title.zh: 卷六 帝紀第六 中宗元帝 肅宗明帝
title.en: Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Yuan; Emperor Ming
title.raw: 卷六 帝紀第六 中宗元帝 肅宗明帝 Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Yuan; Emperor Ming

sentences.zh: 元皇帝諱睿，字景文，宣帝曾孫，琅邪恭王覲之子也。

translations.literal: The Emperor Yuan's taboo name was Rui, his courtesy name Jingwen; he was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Prince Gong of Langye, Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, whose personal name was Rui and courtesy name Jingwen, was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of Jin and the son of Sima Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年生於洛陽，有神光之異，一室盡明，所藉槁如始刈。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianning he was born in Luoyang; there was a divine radiance anomaly; one room was entirely bright; the straw on which he lay was as if newly cut.
translations.idiomatic: He was born in Luoyang in 276, amid a strange glow that lit the whole chamber and left the bedding straw looking freshly mown.

sentences.zh: 及長，白豪生於日角之左，隆準龍顏，目有精曜，顧眄煒如也。

translations.literal: When grown, a white hair grew to the left of his sun-corner; high bridge nose and dragon countenance; his eyes had refined brilliance; his glances were radiant.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he bore a white filament beside the auspicious bump on his forehead, the high-bridged "dragon" profile of a ruler, and eyes so bright that every turn of his gaze seemed to flash with light.

sentences.zh: 年十五，嗣位琅邪王。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he succeeded to the position of Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he inherited the title of Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 幼有令問。

translations.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was already known for an excellent name.

sentences.zh: 及惠皇之際，王室多故，帝每恭儉退讓，以免於禍。

translations.literal: When it came to the time of Emperor Hui, the royal house had many troubles; the emperor each time was respectful, frugal, yielding, in order to avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui, when the house of Jin was rocked by one crisis after another, he habitually kept to modesty, frugality, and deference so as to stay clear of disaster.

sentences.zh: 沈敏有度量，不顯灼然之迹，故時人未之識焉。

translations.literal: Deep and keen, with capacity for tolerance, he did not display glaring traces; therefore people of the time did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: He was steady, astute, and large-minded, yet never advertised his abilities, so his contemporaries failed to see the ruler in him.

sentences.zh: 惟侍中嵇紹異之，謂人曰：「琅邪王毛骨非常，殆非人臣之相也。」

translations.literal: Only Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Shao thought him strange, saying to people: "The Prince of Langye's bearing is extraordinary; probably it is not the appearance of a subject."
translations.idiomatic: Only Ji Shao, the palace attendant, saw something different in him and told others, "The Prince of Langye has a presence no ordinary man possesses; that is hardly the look of someone born to serve another."

sentences.zh: 元康二年，拜員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuankang he was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In 292 he received appointment as supernumerary gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 累遷左將軍，從討成都王穎。

translations.literal: By stages he was promoted to General of the Left and followed in the campaign against the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to general of the left and marched with the army that moved against Sima Ying, prince of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之敗也，叔父東安王繇爲穎所害。

translations.literal: At the defeat at Dangyin, his uncle the Prince of Dong'an, Yao, was killed by Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial forces were shattered at Dangyin, his uncle Sima Yao, prince of Dong'an, fell victim to Ying's purge.

sentences.zh: 帝懼禍及，將出奔。

translations.literal: The emperor feared disaster reaching him and intended to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the blow would soon strike him too, he prepared to slip away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 其夜月正明，而禁衛嚴警，帝無由得去，甚窘迫。

translations.literal: That night the moon was just bright, but the palace guards were strictly alert; the emperor had no means to depart and was very pressed.
translations.idiomatic: The moon shone clear that night, yet the inner-palace cordon was so tight that he could find no way out and grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 有頃，雲霧晦冥，雷雨暴至，徼者皆馳，因得潛出。

translations.literal: After a while, clouds and mist were dark and gloomy; violent rain and thunder arrived; the patrolmen all ran; thereby he was able secretly to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Presently clouds swallowed the moon, a sudden storm broke, and the sentries scattered for shelter, which gave him the opening to steal out unseen.

sentences.zh: 穎先令諸關無得出貴人，帝旣至河陽，爲津吏所止。

translations.literal: Ying had first ordered the various passes not to allow nobles to exit; when the emperor had reached Heyang, he was stopped by the ferry clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had barred every pass to people of rank; when he reached the Heyang ferry a petty official held him up.

sentences.zh: 從者宋典後來，以策鞭帝馬而笑曰：「舍長！

translations.literal: Follower Song Dian came afterward, with a whip struck the emperor's horse and laughed, saying: "Hostel chief!
translations.idiomatic: His follower Song Dian rode up behind him, tapped his mount with a riding crop, and called out with a laugh, "Innkeeper!"

sentences.zh: 官禁貴人，汝亦被拘邪！

translations.literal: The officials forbid nobles; are you also detained!
translations.idiomatic: The authorities are detaining grandees—have they got you as well!

sentences.zh: 」吏乃聽過。

translations.literal: " The clerk then allowed passage.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk, fooled by the act, waved them through.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，迎太妃俱歸國。

translations.literal: Arriving at Luoyang, he welcomed the Grand Consort and together returned to the state.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Luoyang, fetched his mother the grand consort, and escorted her home to his princedom.

sentences.zh: 東海王越之收兵下邳也，假帝輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Donghai, Yue, gathered troops at Xiapi, he provisionally appointed the emperor General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: While Sima Yue, prince of the Eastern Sea, was concentrating his army at Xiapi, he gave him the brevet rank of general who supports the state.

sentences.zh: 尋加平東將軍、監徐州諸軍事，鎮下邳。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed General Who Pacifies the East and supervised military affairs of Xuzhou, garrisoning Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was named general who pacifies the east, put in charge of all military affairs in Xuzhou, and stationed at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 俄遷安東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General Who Guards the East and Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he moved up to general who guards the east and area commander for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 越西迎大駕，留帝居守。

translations.literal: Yue went west to welcome the great chariot, leaving the emperor to remain and guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue marched west to escort the emperor back to the capital, he left him behind to hold the eastern front.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，用王導計，始鎮建鄴，以顧榮爲軍司馬，賀循爲參佐，王敦、王導、周顗、刁協並爲腹心股肱，賓禮名賢，存問風俗，江東歸心焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongjia, using Wang Dao's plan, he first garrisoned Jianye, appointing Gu Rong as army marshal, He Xun as aide; Wang Dun, Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, and Diao Xie together were belly-heart thigh-arm; he guest-treated famous worthies, inquired into customs; the east of the river returned hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongjia era, on Wang Dao's advice, he shifted his headquarters to Jianye. He named Gu Rong army marshal and He Xun as staff officer, while Wang Dun, Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, and Diao Xie formed his inner circle of trusted commanders. He honored local talent, asked after regional ways, and so won the allegiance of the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 屬太妃薨于國，自表奔喪，葬畢，還鎮，增封宣城郡二萬戶，加鎮東大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: It happened that the Grand Consort died in the state; he himself memorialized to rush mourning; when burial was finished, he returned to garrison; his fief was increased by twenty thousand households in Xuancheng commandery; he was added General Who Guards the East, Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother the grand consort died in the princedom he asked leave to go into mourning; after the funeral he returned to his post, received another twenty thousand households in Xuancheng, and was promoted to general who guards the east with the privilege of an independent headquarters equated to the three highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 受越命，討征東將軍周馥，走之。

translations.literal: Receiving Yue's order, he campaigned against General Who Conquers the East Zhou Fu and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: On Yue's orders he attacked Zhou Fu, the general who conquers the east, and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝蒙塵于平陽，司空荀籓等移檄天下，推帝爲盟主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai suffered dust at Pingyang, Minister of Works Xun Fan and others moved proclamations through the realm, pushing the emperor as covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Huai fell captive at Pingyang, Minister of Works Xun Fan and his colleagues circulated a manifesto naming him leader of the loyalist coalition.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史華軼不從，使豫章內史周廣、前江州刺史衛展討禽之。

translations.literal: Governor of Jiangzhou Hua Yi did not obey; he sent Administrator of Yuzhang Zhou Guang and former Governor of Jiangzhou Wei Zhan to campaign and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yi, the Jiangxi governor, refused to fall in line, so he dispatched Zhou Guang of Yuzhang and the former governor Wei Zhan to bring him in by force.

sentences.zh: 愍帝卽位，加左丞相。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, he was added Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min came to the throne he was named left chancellor as well.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，進位丞相、大都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: After more than a year he advanced in rank to Chancellor and Grand Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was raised to full chancellor and grand commander of all forces at court and in the field.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將分定江東，斬叛者孫弼于宣城，平杜弢於湘州，承制赦荊揚。

translations.literal: He dispatched various generals separately to settle the east of the river; he beheaded the rebel Sun Bi at Xuancheng; he pacified Du Tao in Xiangzhou; by imperial commission he pardoned Jing and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals to secure the lower Yangzi region, executed the turncoat Sun Bi at Xuancheng, crushed Du Tao's rising in Hunan, and on delegated authority proclaimed an amnesty for Jingzhou and Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 及西都不守，帝出師露次，躬擐甲胄，移檄四方，徵天下之兵，剋日進討。

translations.literal: When the western capital was not guarded, the emperor went out the army and exposed encampment, personally donned armor and helmet, moved proclamations to the four directions, summoned the realm's troops, set a day to advance and punish.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang'an fell he struck camp in the open field, buckled on his own armor, issued calls to arms across the empire, and mustered every force he could for a timed advance to recover the north.

sentences.zh: 于時有玉册見於臨安，白玉麒麟神璽出於江寧，其文曰「長壽萬年」，日有重暈，皆以爲中興之象焉。

translations.literal: At that time there was a jade document seen at Lin'an; a white jade qilin divine seal emerged at Jiangning; its text said "Long life ten thousand years"; the sun had double halos; all took these as signs of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: About then a jade register was reported at Lin'an, a white jade "qilin" seal turned up at Jiangning bearing the characters 'long life for ten thousand years,' and the sun showed double rings—omens everyone read as proof that the dynasty would rise again.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝素服出次，舉哀三日。

translations.literal: In the third month, the emperor in plain clothes went out to encampment and observed mourning three days.
translations.idiomatic: That third month he donned mourning white, moved his quarters into the field, and kept three days of lament for the fallen capital.

sentences.zh: 西陽王羕及羣僚參佐州征牧守等上尊號，帝不許。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiyang, Yang, and the various officials, aides, provincial shepherds and guards, etc., presented the exalted title; the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yang, prince of Xiyang, together with his staff and the provincial governors, urged him to take the imperial style; he refused.

sentences.zh: 羕等以死固請，至於再三。

translations.literal: Yang and others with death firmly requested, reaching to again and thrice.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed their plea as if their lives hung on it, again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝慨然流涕曰：「孤，罪人也，惟有蹈節死義，以雪天下之恥，庶贖鈇鉞之誅。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and shed tears, saying, "I am a guilty man; only by holding fast to duty and dying for what is right, to wash away the shame upon the realm, might I redeem myself from the axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: With tears in his eyes he said, "I am a criminal in the eyes of the throne. My only path is to keep faith unto death and wipe away this shame upon the world—perhaps then I may escape the headsman's axe.

sentences.zh: 吾本琅邪王，諸賢見逼不已！

translations.literal: I originally am the Prince of Langye; you worthies press me without cease!
translations.idiomatic: I began as nothing more than prince of Langye, yet you gentlemen will not stop forcing me!

sentences.zh: 」乃呼私奴命駕，將反國。

translations.literal: " Then he called a private slave to order the chariot, intending to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: " He shouted for his groom to harness a carriage, as though he meant to ride back to his old fief alone.

sentences.zh: 羣臣乃不敢逼，請依魏晉故事爲晉王，許之。

translations.literal: The host of ministers then did not dare compel; they requested according to Wei-Jin precedent to be Jin Prince; he permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers dared press him no further and asked instead that he accept the title of Prince of Jin after the Wei–Jin precedent; he consented.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，卽王位，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On xinmao he ascended the prince's throne, great amnesty, changed era name.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day he took the princely throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 其殺祖父母、父母，及劉聰、石勒，不從此令。

translations.literal: As for those who killed grandparents, parents, and Liu Cong, Shi Le, they do not follow this order.
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty of parricide and the rebel leaders Liu Cong and Shi Le were excluded from the pardon.

sentences.zh: 諸參軍拜奉車都尉，掾屬駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: The various army advisers were appointed Commandant of the Imperial Coach; the staff subordinates Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: His military advisers were given the nominal rank of commandant of the imperial coach, and his secretarial aides that of commandant of the household cavalry.

sentences.zh: 辟掾屬百餘人，時人謂之「百六掾」。

translations.literal: He summoned staff subordinates over a hundred persons; people of the time called them "hundred-six staff."
translations.idiomatic: He called up more than a hundred clerks to staff his princely administration—contemporaries dubbed them the "hundred and six aides."

sentences.zh: 乃備百官，立宗廟社稷於建康。

translations.literal: Then he completed the hundred officials, established ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He then filled out a full civil service and dedicated the imperial ancestral temple and the altars of soil and grain at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時四方競上符瑞，帝曰：「孤負四海之責，未能思愆，何徵祥之有？」

translations.literal: At the time the four directions competed to present tallies and omens; the emperor said: "I bear the four seas' responsibility, have not been able to think on faults; what auspicious signs are there?"
translations.idiomatic: While the provinces showered him with alleged portents, he replied, "I already shoulder the burden of the realm; I have scarcely begun to reckon my own faults—what right have I to speak of good omens?"

sentences.zh: 丙辰，立世子紹爲晉王太子。

translations.literal: On bingchen he established the heir apparent Shao as Jin Prince Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day he named his heir apparent, Sima Shao, crown prince to the house of Jin.

sentences.zh: 以撫軍大將軍、西陽王羕爲太保，征南大將軍、漢安侯王敦爲大將軍，右將軍王導都督中外諸軍事、驃騎將軍，左長史刁協爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He appointed General Who Garrisons the Army, Prince of Xiyang Yang as Grand Guardian; General Who Conquers the South, Marquis of Han'an Wang Dun as Grand General; General of the Right Wang Dao as Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, General of Agile Cavalry; Left Chief Clerk Diao Xie as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yang, prince of Xiyang, became grand guardian; Wang Dun, marquis of Han'an, grand general; Wang Dao retained command of all armies at court and in the provinces as general of agile cavalry; and Diao Xie, his senior clerk on the left, was made left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 封王子宣城公裒琅邪王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the prince's son Duke of Xuancheng Pou as Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sima Pou, duke of Xuancheng, was invested as the new prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 六月丙寅，司空、幷州刺史、廣武侯劉琨，幽州刺史、左賢王、渤海公段匹磾，領護烏丸校尉、鎮北將軍劉翰，單于、廣甯公段辰，遼西公段眷，冀州刺史、祝阿子劭續，青州刺史、廣饒侯曹嶷，兗州刺史、定襄侯劉演，東夷校尉崔毖，鮮卑大都督慕容廆等一百八十人上書勸進，曰：

translations.literal: On bingyin in the sixth month, Minister of Works, Inspector of Bingzhou, Marquis of Guangwu Liu Kun; Inspector of Youzhou, Worthy King of the Left, Duke of Bohai Duan Pidi; Colonel Who Leads and Protects the Wuhuan, General Who Guards the North Liu Han; Chanyu, Duke of Guangning Duan Chen; Duke of Liaoxi Duan Juan; Inspector of Jizhou, Zhu'a-zi Shao Xu; Inspector of Qingzhou, Marquis of Guangrao Cao Yi; Inspector of Yanzhou, Marquis of Dingxiang Liu Yan; Colonel of the Eastern Yi Cui Bi; Great Commander of the Xianbei Murong Hui, and one hundred eighty others, submitted a memorial urging advancement, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day in the sixth month, Liu Kun—minister of works, governor of Bingzhou, and marquis of Guangwu—joined Duan Pidi, governor of Youzhou and duke of Bohai; Liu Han, Wuhuan commandant and general who guards the north; the chanyu and duke of Guangning, Duan Chen; Duan Juan, duke of Liaoxi; Shao Xu, governor of Jizhou and lord of Zhu'a; Cao Yi, governor of Qingzhou and marquis of Guangrao; Liu Yan, governor of Yanzhou and marquis of Dingxiang; Cui Bi, colonel of the eastern Yi; Murong Hui, commander-in-chief of the Xianbei; and one hundred seventy-two other notables in a joint memorial pressing him to take the throne. They wrote:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天生蒸民，樹之以君，所以對越天地，司牧黎元。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard that Heaven produced the multitude of people and established for them a ruler, whereby to respond to and go beyond Heaven and Earth and to shepherd the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: We have read that Heaven bred the common people and set a sovereign over them so that he might answer to Heaven and Earth and care for all who live under their sky.

sentences.zh: 聖帝明王監其若此，知天地不可以乏饗，故屈其身以奉之；

translations.literal: Sage emperors and enlightened kings observed it thus: they knew Heaven and Earth could not lack offerings; therefore they bent their persons to serve them;
translations.idiomatic: The sage-kings of old saw this pattern: the spirits of Heaven and Earth must receive their due, so they humbled themselves in the ritual service of the altars;

sentences.zh: 知蒸黎不可以無主，故不得已而臨之。

translations.literal: they knew the multitude could not lack a lord; therefore they unavoidably faced it.
translations.idiomatic: and they knew the people could not long be without a head, which is why they took the throne only when they had no honorable choice.

sentences.zh: 社稷時難，則戚藩定其傾；

translations.literal: When altars of soil and grain met timely hardship, then kin-princes settled its overturning;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the altars tottered, it was a prince of the blood who righted the tilt;

sentences.zh: 郊廟或替，則宗哲纂其祀。

translations.literal: when suburban and temple sacrifices were perhaps replaced, then clan-wise ones continued their sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: when the suburban rites faltered, a wise kinsman always stepped forward to keep the ancestral fire burning.

sentences.zh: 是以弘振遐風，式固萬世，三五以降，靡不由之。

translations.literal: Therefore they broadly stirred distant winds, thereby securing ten thousand generations; from the Three and Five down, none have not followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they spread their transforming influence to the farthest marches and bound the dynasty for ages to come—since the legendary Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, no true king has acted otherwise.

sentences.zh: 伏惟高祖宣皇帝肇基景命，世祖武皇帝遂造區夏，三葉重光，四聖繼軌，惠澤侔於有虞，卜世過於周氏。

translations.literal: We humbly consider: High Ancestor Emperor Xuan founded the bright mandate; Ancestor Emperor Wu then built the central summer; three leaves repeated radiance; four sages continued the track; favor and moisture matched Youyu; divined generations exceeded the Zhou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Your house began when Emperor Xuan received the great mandate, and Emperor Wu brought all within the Xia heartland under one rule; three generations shone anew, four sagely sovereigns walked in one another's footsteps; their kindness rivaled that of Shun's age, and Heaven granted your line more years of fortune than ever blessed the house of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 自元康以來，艱難繁興，永嘉之際，氛厲彌昏，宸極失御，登遐醜裔，國家之危，有若綴旒。

translations.literal: From Yuankang onward, hardships repeatedly arose; at the Yongjia juncture, miasma and pestilence grew ever darker; the polar throne lost control; ascended distant ugly descendants; the state's danger was like dangling tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuankang era troubles have multiplied; by Yongjia the air itself seemed poisoned with rebellion. The Son of Heaven lost his grip, barbarian pretenders seized the capital, and the dynasty hung by a thread like the king's tassels swaying over his brow.

sentences.zh: 賴先后之德、宗廟之靈，皇帝嗣建，舊物克甄。

translations.literal: Relying on former empresses' virtue and the ancestral temple's numen, the emperor succeeded in establishment; old things were able to be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Through the virtue of your ancestresses and the blessing of the imperial shrines, a new sovereign was raised and the old regalia of Jin began to shine again.

sentences.zh: 誕授欽明，服膺聰哲，玉質幼彰，金聲夙振。

translations.literal: He was granted reverent brilliance; he took to heart wisdom and discernment; his jade-like quality showed even in youth; his metal-clear reputation rang out early.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven gave him a luminous mind; he cherished wisdom and keen judgment, and even as a boy the polish of jade and the ring of bronze in his speech marked him as the true heir.

sentences.zh: 冢宰攝其綱，百辟輔其政，四海想中興之美，羣生懷來蘇之望。

translations.literal: The grand steward grasped its net; the hundred lords assisted his government; the four seas longed for restoration's beauty; the multitude of creatures cherished the hope of coming-to-life.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister held the reins, the nobles rallied to his government, and every corner of the realm looked for the splendor of a second founding, while the people clung to the hope of revival spoken of in the old odes.

sentences.zh: 不圖天不悔禍，大災薦臻，國未忘難，寇害尋興。

translations.literal: We did not reckon Heaven would not repent disaster; great calamities repeatedly arrived; the state had not forgotten hardship; bandit harm soon arose.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven did not relent: fresh disasters followed hard upon the last, the wounds of the state had scarcely closed when new invaders struck.

sentences.zh: 逆胡劉曜，縱逸西都，敢肆犬羊，陵虐天邑。

translations.literal: The rebellious Hu Liu Yao, released and unrestrained in the western capital, dared to unleash dogs and sheep, encroaching and oppressing the heavenly city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Liu Yao ran wild in the western capital, behaving like a wolf in the fold and trampling the sacred precincts of the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣奉表使還，乃承西朝以去年十一月不守，主上幽劫，復沈虜庭，神器流離，再辱荒逆。

translations.literal: Your subject, presenting a memorial envoy returning, then received that the western court in last year's eleventh month was not guarded; the lord above was secluded and seized; again he sank in the barbarian court; the divine vessel drifted apart; twice humiliated by wild rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When your servant's embassy returned from the west, we learned that Chang'an had fallen the previous winter: our sovereign was dragged back into captivity, the imperial regalia scattered abroad, and the sacred throne dishonored a second time by barbarian usurpers.

sentences.zh: 臣每覽史籍，觀之前載，厄運之極，古今未有。

translations.literal: Your subject each time peruses the historical records, observing the former records; the extreme of ill fortune, ancient and modern, has not had it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever we turn the pages of history we find nothing—ancient or modern—that matches this depth of calamity.

sentences.zh: 苟在食土之毛，含血之類，莫不叩心絕氣，行號巷哭。

translations.literal: If among those who eat the soil's hair, blood-containing kinds, none do not strike the heart and cut off breath, walking wailing and lane weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Every creature that draws breath and lives on this soil beats its breast till breath fails and wanders the lanes in lament.

sentences.zh: 況臣等荷寵三世，位廁鼎司，聞問震惶，精爽飛越，且驚且惋，五情無主，舉哀朔垂，上下泣血。

translations.literal: How much more your subjects and others bearing favor three generations, positions attending the tripod ministers, hearing the news were shaken in terror, essence and brightness flew beyond, both alarmed and grieved, five emotions without master, raising mourning at the northern fringe, above and below weeping blood.
translations.idiomatic: How much more we who have enjoyed three generations of imperial favor and stood among the highest ministers: the news struck us senseless with grief and dread; our wits scattered; we mourned toward the lost north until eyes and hearts alike seemed to weep blood.

sentences.zh: 臣聞昏明迭用，否泰相濟，天命無改，曆數有歸。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard that dark and bright alternate in use, obstruction and peace aid each other; Heaven's mandate is without change; the reckoned succession has a return.
translations.idiomatic: We are taught that night yields to day, misfortune to ease, while Heaven's mandate stands unshaken and the turn of the dynastic cycle always finds its rightful heir.

sentences.zh: 或多難以固邦國，或殷憂以啓聖明。

translations.literal: Sometimes many hardships thereby firm the state; sometimes deep sorrow thereby opens sagely brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Often it is a flood of trials that steels a kingdom, or crushing sorrow that awakens a sage.

sentences.zh: 是以齊有無知之禍，而小白爲五伯之長；

translations.literal: Therefore Qi had the disaster of Wuzhi, yet Xiaobai became chief of the Five Hegemons;
translations.idiomatic: Qi survived the coup of Wuzhi only to see Duke Huan rise as first among the Five Hegemons;

sentences.zh: 晉有麗姬之難，而重耳以主諸侯之盟。

translations.literal: Jin had Lady Li's hardship, yet Chong'er thereby presided over the lords' covenant.
translations.idiomatic: and Jin weathered Lady Li's intrigue until Duke Wen held the covenant of the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 社稷靡安，必將有以扶其危；

translations.literal: When altars of soil and grain are not at peace, there must be something thereby to support its danger;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the altars totter, Heaven always sends someone to shore them up;

sentences.zh: 黔首幾絕，必將有以繼其緒。

translations.literal: when the black-haired are nearly cut off, there must be something thereby to continue its thread.
translations.idiomatic: when the people stand at the brink of extinction, Heaven always raises a man to carry on the line.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，玄德通于神明，聖姿合於兩儀，應命世之期，紹千載之運。

translations.literal: We humbly consider Your Majesty: dark virtue penetrates to spirits and gods; sagely form accords with the Two Powers; you answer the age of the ordained mandate; you continue a thousand years' fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's subtle virtue moves spirits and gods; your bearing answers Heaven and Earth; you have come in the very hour fate demands and taken up a mandate a thousand years in the making.

sentences.zh: 符瑞之表，天人有徵；

translations.literal: The manifestation of tallies and omens, Heaven and man have signs;
translations.idiomatic: The portents that have appeared are proof enough that Heaven and humanity are of one mind;

sentences.zh: 中興之兆，圖讖垂典。

translations.literal: the omens of restoration, charts and prophecies hang down as canons.
translations.idiomatic: and every chart and prophecy handed down from antiquity points to this restoration.

sentences.zh: 自京畿隕喪，九服崩離，天下囂然，無所歸懷，雖有夏之遘夷羿，宗姬之離犬戎，蔑以過之。

translations.literal: Since the capital region's fall and loss, the nine domains collapsed and parted; the realm was clamorous, without place to return the heart; although Xia suffered the usurpation of the archer Yi and the house of Zhou was driven out by the Dog Rong, nothing has exceeded this.
translations.idiomatic: Since the heartland fell the nine provinces have shattered and the empire roams uprooted with nowhere to lay its loyalty. The barbarian Yi who seized Xia and the Quanrong who drove out the Zhou were trifles beside this.

sentences.zh: 陛下撫征江左，奄有舊吳，柔服以德，伐叛以刑，抗明威以攝不類，杖大順以號宇內。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has soothed and campaigned south of the Yangzi, covering the old Wu; you soften submission with virtue; you punish rebels with the law; you oppose bright awesomeness to awe the unkind; you staff great compliance to command within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: You have rallied the south of the Yangzi, reunited the old lands of Wu, won allegiance with kindness, struck rebels with the law, let your majesty overawe the wicked, and wielded righteous authority to call the realm to order.

sentences.zh: 純化旣敷，則率土宅心；

translations.literal: When pure transformation is already spread, then all within the soil lodge their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Your transforming influence spreads, and every soil clings to you as its heart;

sentences.zh: 義風旣暢，則遐方企踵。

translations.literal: when righteous wind is already smooth, then distant regions stand on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: your righteous example runs abroad, and distant peoples stand on tiptoe hoping for your rule.

sentences.zh: 百揆時敘于上，四門穆穆于下。

translations.literal: The hundred affairs were timely ordered above; the four gates were solemn below.
translations.idiomatic: Above, every branch of government fell into harmony; below, the four gates of the court stood in august stillness.

sentences.zh: 昔少康之隆，夏訓以爲美談；

translations.literal: Formerly Shaokang's flourishing, Xia instructions took as fine discourse;
translations.idiomatic: The restoration of Shaokang is still praised in the lessons of Xia;

sentences.zh: 宣王中興，周詩以爲休詠。

translations.literal: King Xuan's restoration, Zhou odes took as auspicious chant.
translations.idiomatic: and King Xuan's revival became the glad theme of the Odes of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 況茂勳格於皇天，清暉光于四海，蒼生顒然，莫不欣戴，聲教所加，願爲臣妾者哉！

translations.literal: How much more abundant merit reaching to August Heaven, clear radiance shining on the four seas; the black-haired look up; none do not joyfully support; where sound and teaching reach, who would not wish to be subject and concubine!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when your towering merit moves High Heaven, your pure light floods the four seas, and the common people lift their faces in hope—who under the reach of your transforming influence would not gladly call himself your subject!

sentences.zh: 且宣皇之胤，惟有陛下，憶兆攸歸，曾無與二。

translations.literal: Moreover of Emperor Xuan's descendants, only is Your Majesty; the hundred million's belonging, absolutely none with a second.
translations.idiomatic: Among the posterity of Emperor Xuan you alone survive, and the allegiance of millions rests on no second name.

sentences.zh: 天祚大晉，必將有主，主晉祀者，非陛下而誰！

translations.literal: Heaven's blessing on great Jin, there must be a lord; he who masters Jin's sacrifices—if not Your Majesty, then who!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven will not leave Great Jin without a master, and who but Your Majesty can tend the altars of the house of Sima!

sentences.zh: 是以邇無異言，遠無異望，謳歌者無不吟諷徽猷，獄訟者無不思於聖德。

translations.literal: Therefore near has no different words, far has no different hopes; singers have none who do not chant and intone fine plans; litigants have none who do not think on sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Hence none near speaks with two voices and none far harbors a rival hope: every song extols your wise design, and every quarrel in the market is hushed by thoughts of your virtue.

sentences.zh: 天地之際旣交，華夷之情允洽。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth's border is already joined; Chinese and barbarian feelings are truly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are in accord again, and Chinese and barbarian hearts beat as one.

sentences.zh: 一角之獸，連理之木，以爲休徵者，蓋有百數。

translations.literal: One-horned beasts, trees of joined trunks, taken as auspicious signs, are perhaps in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: The unicorns, the trees whose branches grow as one—such tokens of blessing have been reported by the hundred.

sentences.zh: 冠帶之倫，要荒之衆，不謀同辭者，動以萬計。

translations.literal: Those of cap-and-belt class, the multitudes of yao and huang, not plotting yet same words, move by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry of the inner provinces and chieftains of the outer marches, though strangers to one another, speak with a single voice, and their memorials are counted in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 是以臣等敢考天地之心，因函夏之趣，昧死上尊號。

translations.literal: Therefore your subjects and others dare examine Heaven and Earth's hearts, following the Xia-in-a-box's tendency, blindly risk death to present the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we have ventured to read the mind of Heaven and Earth and the temper of the heartland, and at peril of our lives we present this exalted title.

sentences.zh: 願陛下存舜禹至公之情，狹由巢抗矯之節；

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty to preserve Shun and Yu's utmost public feeling, to narrow You and Chao's stiff integrity;
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to keep the selfless public spirit of Shun and Yu, and set aside the narrow scruples of recluse hermits;

sentences.zh: 以社稷爲務，不以小行爲先；

translations.literal: take altars of soil and grain as task, not take small conduct as first;
translations.idiomatic: to put the altars first, not petty personal modesty;

sentences.zh: 以黔首爲憂，不以克讓爲事；

translations.literal: take the black-haired as worry, not take able yielding as affair;
translations.idiomatic: to fret for the black-haired millions rather than for the reputation of yielding the throne;

sentences.zh: 上尉宗廟乃顧之懷，下釋普天傾首之勤。

translations.literal: Above comfort the ancestral temple's thus-looking heart; below release all-under-Heaven's bowing-head toil.
translations.idiomatic: thus you would ease the anxious dead who watch from the shrines and lift from the people the weary craning of their necks toward you.

sentences.zh: 則所謂生繁華于枯荑，育豐肌于朽骨，神人獲安，無不幸甚。

translations.literal: Then what is called producing splendor on withered sprouts, nurturing rich flesh on rotten bones, spirits and men obtain peace, none not greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Then indeed you would make the dead stem bloom again and put flesh on dry bones—spirits and mortals alike would find peace, and none would count himself less than blessed.

sentences.zh: 臣聞尊位不可久虛，萬機不可久曠。

translations.literal: Your subjects have heard the honored position cannot long be empty; the myriad threads cannot long be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: We are told that the throne must not long stand vacant nor the myriad affairs of state long lie unattended.

sentences.zh: 虛之一日，則尊位以殆；

translations.literal: If empty one day, then the honored position thereby is endangered;
translations.idiomatic: A single day's vacancy puts the supreme seat in peril;

sentences.zh: 曠之浹辰，則萬機以亂。

translations.literal: if neglected a full ten days, then the myriad threads thereby are chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: ten days of neglect throws every branch of government into confusion.

sentences.zh: 方今踵百王之季，當陽九之會，狡寇窺窬，伺國瑕隙，黎元波蕩，無所繫心，安可廢而不恤哉？

translations.literal: Now following the hundred kings' end, meeting the yang-nine's conjunction, crafty bandits peep and crawl, wait for the state's crack; the black-haired wave and toss, without place to tie the heart—how can one abandon and not pity?
translations.idiomatic: We stand in the twilight of the dynasties, in the hour of fate's harshest reckoning: rebels watch for every crack in the armor of the state, and the people drift like flotsam with nothing to cling to—how can the throne be left empty and the realm unwatched?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲逡巡，其若宗廟何？

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty may wish to hesitate and hold back, what of the ancestral temple?
translations.idiomatic: Even if you mean to hang back, what will become of the imperial shrines?

sentences.zh: 其若百姓何？

translations.literal: What of the hundred surnames?
translations.idiomatic: What is to become of the common people?

sentences.zh: 昔者惠公虜秦，晉國震駭，呂郤之謀，欲立子圉，外以絕敵人之志，內以固闔境之情。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Hui was captured at Qin; the state of Jin was shaken; Lü and Xi's plot wished to establish Zi Yu; outwardly thereby to cut off the enemy's intent, inwardly thereby to firm the feelings within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Hui of Jin fell captive in Qin, the court reeled; Lü and Xi plotted to put Prince Yu on the throne—both to break the enemy's will abroad and to steady hearts at home.

sentences.zh: 故曰「喪君有君，羣臣輯睦，好我者勸，惡我者懼」。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, "Though the lord be lost, there is a lord; the host of ministers is harmonious; those who favor us are encouraged; those who hate us are fearful."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "A state may lose its ruler yet still have a ruler; when ministers pull together, friends take heart and foes grow afraid."

sentences.zh: 前事之不忘，後代之元龜也。

translations.literal: Not forgetting former affairs is the great tortoise of later generations.
translations.idiomatic: To remember the past is to hold the mirror that guides the future.

sentences.zh: 陛下明並日月，無幽不燭，深謀遠猷，出自胸懷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's brightness matches sun and moon; there is no dark place not illuminated; deep plans and distant schemes issue from the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Your clarity rivals sun and moon—no corner stays hidden—and the far-reaching designs you frame come straight from a sovereign heart.

sentences.zh: 不勝犬馬憂國之情，遲睹人神開泰之路，是以陳其乃誠，布之執事。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the dog-horse feeling of worrying for the state, delaying to see the path by which men and spirits open to peace; therefore we display this utmost sincerity, spreading it to those who hold office.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot contain the loyal servant's ache for the realm, nor our longing to see men and gods tread again the road of peace; therefore we lay bare our hearts before those who govern.

sentences.zh: 臣等忝于方任，久在遐外，不得陪列闕庭，與睹盛禮，踴躍之懷，南望罔極。

translations.literal: Your subjects and others disgracefully occupy regional charge, long have been in distant outer regions, unable to attend arrayed at the palace gate, together to witness the grand rites; the leaping-in-the-heart feeling, gazing south has no limit.
translations.idiomatic: We are unworthy men holding frontier posts, far from the capital and barred from the great ceremony; our hearts leap with hope, yet as we gaze southward there is no end to the distance.

sentences.zh: 帝優令答之。

translations.literal: The emperor with a gracious edict answered them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 語在《琨傳》。

translations.literal: The wording is recorded in Liu Kun's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's reply in full is narrated in the biography of Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 石勒將石季龍圍譙城，平西將軍祖逖擊走之。

translations.literal: Shi Le's general Shi Jilong besieged Qiao city; General Who Pacifies the West Zu Ti attacked and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, a general under Shi Le, besieged Qiao, but Zu Ti, the general who pacifies the west, struck and forced him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 己巳，帝傅檄天下曰：「逆賊石勒，肆虐河朔，逋誅歷載，遊魂縱逸。

translations.literal: On jisi the emperor transmitted a proclamation through the realm, saying: "The rebellious bandit Shi Le, violently oppresses Hebei; fleeing punishment for years, his wandering soul is released and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day he circulated a manifesto: "The rebel Shi Le has ravaged the north for years, eluding execution while his hosts roam at will."

sentences.zh: 復遣凶黨石季龍犬羊之衆，越河南渡，縱其鴆毒。

translations.literal: Again he sent the vicious partisan Shi Jilong at the head of a rabble like dogs and sheep; they crossed the Yellow River southward and unleashed their poison.
translations.idiomatic: He has again sent Shi Hu at the head of a brute herd across the river to work their malice on the southern bank.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍祖逖帥衆討擊，應時潰散。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Zu Ti led the multitude to campaign and strike; in response to the moment they scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti, general who pacifies the west, led his men against them and broke their host at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 今遣車騎將軍，琅邪王裒等九軍，銳卒三萬，水陸四道，逕造賊場，受逖節度。

translations.literal: Now dispatching the general of chariots and cavalry, the Prince of Langye Pou, with eight other commands—nine armies in all—thirty thousand crack troops by four routes, water and land, proceeding straight to the bandit camp, all to obey Zu's orders.
translations.idiomatic: I now send Sima Pou, prince of Langye and general of chariots and cavalry, at the head of nine armies—thirty thousand picked men advancing by four routes, by water and land—straight into the rebel stronghold, every column answering to Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 有能梟季龍首者。

translations.literal: If there is one able to display Jilong's head.
translations.idiomatic: Let any man who can bring in Shi Hu's head come forward.

sentences.zh: 賞絹三千匹，金五十斤，封縣侯，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Reward silk three thousand bolts, gold fifty jin, enfeoff as county marquis, fief households two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He shall receive three thousand bolts of silk, fifty catties of gold, a county marquisate, and a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又賊黨能梟送季龍首，封賞亦同之。」

translations.literal: Moreover if members of the rebel faction are able to deliver Jilong's head, enfeoffment and rewards shall be the same."
translations.idiomatic: The same titles and gifts shall go to any traitor in his ranks who brings in Shi Hu's head."

sentences.zh: 七月，散騎侍郎朱嵩、尚書郎顧球卒，帝痛之，將爲舉哀。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Cavalier Gentleman Zhu Song and Secretariat Gentleman Gu Qiu died; the emperor grieved for them and was about to hold mourning for them.
translations.idiomatic: That seventh month the gentlemen Zhu Song and Gu Qiu died; the emperor mourned them deeply and prepared to order court lamentation.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，舊尚書郎不在舉哀之例。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: by precedent Secretariat gentlemen are not within the category of holding mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry reported that by old rule secretariat clerks were not entitled to a state funeral.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「衰亂之弊，特相痛悼。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the harms of decline and chaos, especially mutually grieve."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "These are times of ruin; I mourn them the more keenly."

sentences.zh: 」於是遂舉哀，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: " Thereupon then held mourning; wept for them very bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore ordered the court into mourning and wept for them with uncommon grief.

sentences.zh: 丁未，梁王悝薨。

translations.literal: On dingwei the Prince of Liang, Kui, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day Sima Kui, prince of Liang, died.

sentences.zh: 以太尉荀組爲司徒。

translations.literal: He appointed Grand Commandant Xun Zu as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Xun Zu was named minister of education.

sentences.zh: 弛山澤之禁。

translations.literal: He relaxed the prohibitions on mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Restrictions on logging and foraging in the hills and lakes were lifted.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，封梁王世子翹爲梁王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on jiawu he enfeoffed the Prince of Liang's heir apparent Qiao as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day in the eighth month the heir apparent of Liang, Sima Qiao, succeeded as prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史第五猗爲賊帥杜曾所推，遂與曾同反。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jingzhou Diwu Yi was pushed by bandit chief Du Zeng; thereupon together with Zeng alike rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Yi, governor of Jingzhou, was manipulated by the rebel leader Du Zeng and joined him in revolt.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅，王敦使武昌太守趙誘、襄陽太守朱軌、陵江將軍黃峻討猗，爲其將杜曾所敗，誘等皆死之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on wuyin Wang Dun sent Wuchang Administrator Zhao You, Xiangyang Administrator Zhu Gui, General Who Fords the River Huang Jun to campaign against Yi; they were defeated by his general Du Zeng; You and the others all died for it.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day in the ninth month Wang Dun ordered Zhao You of Wuchang, Zhu Gui of Xiangyang, and the river-fording general Huang Jun against Diwu Yi; Du Zeng routed them and Zhao You and his colleagues were killed.

sentences.zh: 石勒害京兆太守華諝。

translations.literal: Shi Le harmed Jingzhao Administrator Hua Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le executed Hua Xu, the governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史周訪討杜曾，大破之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhou Fang campaigned against Du Zeng and greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang, governor of Liangzhou, attacked Du Zeng and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 十月丁未，琅邪王裒薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month on dingwei the Prince of Langye, Pou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day in the tenth month Sima Pou, prince of Langye, died.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲子，封汝南王子弼爲新蔡王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on jiazi he enfeoffed the Prince of Runan's son Bi as Prince of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day in the eleventh month the emperor invested Sima Bi, a son of the prince of Runan, as prince of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以司空劉琨爲太尉。

translations.literal: On dingmao he appointed Minister of Works Liu Kun as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day Liu Kun was moved from minister of works to grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 置史官，立太學。

translations.literal: He established historiographers; he established the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He instituted the office of court historian and founded the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 是歲，揚州大旱。

translations.literal: That year Yangzhou had great drought.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yangzhou suffered a severe drought.

sentences.zh: 太興元年春正月戊申朔，臨朝，懸而不樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixing, spring first month, wushen new moon, he faced the court; suspended but without music.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 318, on the new-moon day wushen, he held court with bells stilled and no music played.

sentences.zh: 三月癸丑，愍帝崩問至，帝斬縗居廬。

translations.literal: In the third month on guichou news of Emperor Min's death arrived; the emperor wore severed hemp and dwelt in the hut.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the third month word came that Emperor Min was dead; he donned the coarsest mourning sackcloth and moved into the mourning shed.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，百僚上尊號。

translations.literal: On bingchen the hundred officials presented the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day the high ministers presented him with the imperial style.

sentences.zh: 令曰：「孤以不德，當厄運之極，臣節未立，匡救未舉，夙夜所以忘寢食也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I, lacking virtue, face the extreme of ill fortune; subject integrity is not yet established; rescue is not yet raised; day and night therefore forget sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: His rescript ran: "I am a man of small virtue caught at the worst pass of fate; I have not yet proved myself a loyal servant nor brought deliverance to the throne—night and day I forget to eat or sleep."

sentences.zh: 今宗廟廢絕，億兆無系，羣官庶尹，咸勉之以大政，亦何敢辭，輒敬從所執。

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temple is cut off and ended; the hundred million lack attachment; the host of officials and multitude of directors all press him with the great government; how dare I decline; respectfully I follow what is held.
translations.idiomatic: Now the shrines stand empty and the people have no pole star; every minister urges the great charge upon me. How could I refuse? I bow and accept what you press upon me."

sentences.zh: 」是日，卽皇帝位。

translations.literal: " That day he ascended the emperor's position.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he mounted the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔我高祖宣皇帝誕應期運，廓開王基。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Formerly our High Ancestor Emperor Xuan was born responding to the period's fortune, broadly opened the kingly foundation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Long ago my high ancestor Emperor Xuan answered Heaven's call and laid the foundations of our kingship.

sentences.zh: 景、文皇帝奕世重光，緝熙諸夏。

translations.literal: Emperors Jing and Wen, generation after generation repeated radiance, gathered brightness over the various Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Jing and Wen renewed the dynasty's light and brought good order to the heartland of Xia.

sentences.zh: 爰暨世祖，應天順時，受茲明命。

translations.literal: Then reaching the Shizu, he answered Heaven and followed the times, received this bright mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Then came my ancestor Emperor Wu, who obeyed Heaven and the hour and received this luminous charge.

sentences.zh: 功格天地，仁濟宇宙。

translations.literal: Merit reached Heaven and Earth; benevolence aided the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: His merit spanned Heaven and Earth; his kindness reached to the bounds of the world.

sentences.zh: 昊天不融，降此鞠凶，懷帝短世，越去王都。

translations.literal: Vast Heaven was not harmonious; sent down this great calamity; Emperor Huai's short generation, crossed away from the kingly capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yet August Heaven withheld its favor and sent down this crushing evil: Emperor Huai's reign was cut short and he was driven from the royal capital.

sentences.zh: 天禍薦臻，大行皇帝崩殂，社稷無奉。

translations.literal: Heaven's calamities repeatedly arrived; the great departed emperor collapsed; the altars of soil and grain had none to serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster followed disaster until the late emperor passed away and the altars of state were left untended.

sentences.zh: 肆羣后三司六事之人，疇咨庶尹，至于華戎，致葺大命於朕躬。

translations.literal: Therefore the host of lords, the three offices, the six affairs' men, consulted the multitude of directors, reaching to Chinese and barbarian, caused to repair the great mandate upon my person.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the feudal lords, the three high ministers, and the heads of the six boards, together with every governor and even leaders of Chinese and barbarian, have urged the great mandate upon my person.

sentences.zh: 予一人畏天之威，用弗敢違。

translations.literal: I alone fear Heaven's awesomeness; therefore dare not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: I stand alone in awe of Heaven's majesty and dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 遂登壇南獄，受終文祖，焚柴頒瑞，告類上帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon ascended the altar at the southern marchmount, received the end from Wen Ancestor, burned kindling and issued auspicious signs, informed categories to High Lord.
translations.idiomatic: So I ascended the southern altar, received the abdication as did the kings of old before the spirit of King Wen, burned the offering kindling, displayed the auspicious tokens, and reported to High Heaven according to the rite.

sentences.zh: 惟朕寡德，纘我洪緒，若涉大川，罔知攸濟。

translations.literal: Only I scant virtue, continue my great thread, as if fording a great river, know not where to cross.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of slender virtue who must carry on a mighty line; I am like one who faces a wide river without knowing where to find a ford.

sentences.zh: 惟爾股肱爪牙之佐，文武熊羆之臣，用能弼寧晉室，輔余一人。

translations.literal: Only you thigh-arm claw-fang assistants, civil and military bear-pi ministers, thereby able to assist and pacify the Jin house, aid my lone person.
translations.idiomatic: I look to you—my arms and claws, my civil and military ministers bold as bears—to steady the house of Jin and to uphold me, the solitary man above all.

sentences.zh: 思與萬國，共同休慶。

translations.literal: I think to share with the myriad states together the same rest and celebration.
translations.idiomatic: May I share this hour of peace and blessing with every land within the four seas."

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦，改元，文武增位二等。

translations.literal: " Thereupon great amnesty, changed era name, civil and military increased rank two grades.
translations.idiomatic: " He then proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted a new reign title, and raised civil and military officials two steps in rank.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立王太子紹爲皇太子。

translations.literal: On gengwu he established the king's heir apparent Shao as imperial heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day he named his heir apparent, Sima Shao, crown prince of the empire.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔曰：「昔之爲政者，動人以行不以言，應天以實不以文，故我清靜而人自正。

translations.literal: On renshen an edict said: "Of old those who governed moved people by deeds not by words, answered Heaven by substance not by ornament; therefore I am pure and still and people correct themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day he issued an edict: "The ancients moved the people by deeds, not speeches; they answered Heaven with substance, not show. Hence in my stillness the people set themselves aright.

sentences.zh: 其次聽言觀行，明試以功。

translations.literal: Next listen to words and observe deeds, clearly test by merit.
translations.idiomatic: Next they listened to what men said and watched what they did, testing merit in the clear light of day.

sentences.zh: 其有政績可述，刑獄得中，人無怨訟，久而日新，及當官軟弱，茹柔吐剛，行身穢濁，修飾時譽者，各以名聞。

translations.literal: As for those who have administrative traces worth narrating, punishments and prisons hit the mean, people have no resentful lawsuits, long yet daily renewed, and those who hold office are weak and soft, swallow soft and spit hard, conduct body filthy turbid, cultivate adornment for timely fame—each by name report.
translations.idiomatic: Let every governor report by name those whose record deserves praise—where justice is even, the people are free of bitter suits, and government grows fresher with the years—as well as those who are timid in office, bully the weak while truckling to the strong, live corrupt lives, or chase hollow reputation.

sentences.zh: 令在事之人，仰鑒前烈，同心戮力，深思所以寬衆息役，惠益百姓，無廢朕命。

translations.literal: Order those who are in affairs to look up and mirror former ardent ones, with one heart join strength, deeply think how thereby to widen the multitude and rest corvée, benefit and aid the hundred surnames; do not neglect my command.
translations.idiomatic: All who hold office shall take the great ministers of old as their mirror, work with one heart, think hard how to ease the burdens of the people and bring them real good, and not treat my command lightly.

sentences.zh: 遠近禮贄，一切斷之。」

translations.literal: Near and far ritual gifts, all cut them off."
translations.idiomatic: Gifts sent from near or far as court courtesy are hereby forbidden altogether."

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, dingchou new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, on the new-moon day dingchou, the sun was partially eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 加大將軍王敦江州牧，進驃騎將軍王導開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He added Grand General Wang Dun as Governor of Jiangzhou; promoted General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao to Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Wang Dun was given the added title of governor of Jiangzhou, and Wang Dao, general of agile cavalry, was advanced to independent command with honors equal to the three highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，初禁招魂葬。

translations.literal: On wuyin he first forbade soul-summoning burials.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day he issued the first ban on "soul-calling" burials where no body was present.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，西平地震。

translations.literal: On yiyou Xiping had an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day the earth shook at Xiping.

sentences.zh: 五月癸丑，使持節、侍中、都督、太尉、幷州刺史、廣武侯劉琨爲段匹磾所害。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on guichou, Bearer of the Scepter, Palace Attendant, Area Commander, Grand Commandant, Inspector of Bingzhou, Marquis of Guangwu Liu Kun was killed by Duan Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the fifth month Liu Kun—bearing the imperial insignia, palace attendant, area commander, grand commandant, governor of Bingzhou, and marquis of Guangwu—was murdered by Duan Pidi.

sentences.zh: 六月，旱，帝親雩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month there was drought; the emperor personally performed the yu rain sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth month brought drought, and the emperor led the great rain prayer himself.

sentences.zh: 改丹陽內史爲丹陽尹。

translations.literal: He changed Danyang Administrator to Danyang Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: The title of Danyang administrator was changed to Danyang intendant.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以尚書左僕射刁協爲尚書令，平南將軍、曲陵公荀崧爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On jiashen he appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Diao Xie as Director of the Secretariat; General Who Pacifies the South, Marquis of Quling Xun Song as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day Diao Xie rose from left vice director to director of the secretariat, while Xun Song, the general who pacifies the south and marquis of Quling, was named left vice director.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以滎陽太守李矩爲都督司州諸軍事、司州刺史。

translations.literal: On gengyin he appointed Xingyang Administrator Li Ju as Area Commander-in-Chief of Sizhou military affairs, Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day Li Ju, governor of Xingyang, was put in command of all military affairs in Sizhou and given the governorship of that province.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，封皇子晞爲武陵王。

translations.literal: On wuxu he enfeoffed the imperial son Xi as Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day the emperor's son Sima Xi was invested as prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 初置諫鼓謗木。

translations.literal: He first established remonstrance drum and slander wood.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time he set up the complaint drum and the suggestion board of ancient model.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊申，詔曰：「王室多故，姦凶肆暴，皇綱馳墜，顛覆大猷。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, wushen, an edict said: "The royal house has many causes; wicked and fierce wildly commit violence; the imperial net gallops and falls; overturn the great plan.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the seventh month an edict read: "The house of Jin has suffered blow after blow; villains run riot; the cords of rule have slackened and the great design lies overturned.

sentences.zh: 朕以不德，統承洪緒，夙夜憂危，思改其弊。

translations.literal: I, lacking virtue, inherit and receive the great thread; day and night worry in peril, think to reform its harms.
translations.idiomatic: I lack virtue yet have inherited the great line; night and day I fret over these ills and seek a way to mend them.

sentences.zh: 二千石令長當祗奉舊憲，正身明法，抑齊豪強，存恤孤獨，隱實戶口，勸課農桑。

translations.literal: Two-thousand-bushel commanders and magistrates ought reverently to uphold old statutes, correct the body and clarify the law, suppress and equalize powerful magnates, preserve and pity orphans and solitaries, conceal and verify household registers, encourage and supervise farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Every governor and county magistrate must uphold the standing laws, keep his own conduct straight, hold the rich and powerful in check, care for widows and orphans, bring hidden households back on the rolls, and urge farming and silk work.

sentences.zh: 州牧刺史當互相檢察，不得顧私虧公。

translations.literal: Shepherds and inspectors ought mutually to inspect and watch; must not look to private loss to the public.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governors shall watch one another and never put private interest ahead of the public good.

sentences.zh: 長吏有志在奉公而不見進用者，有貪惏穢濁而以財勢自安者，若有不舉，當受故縱蔽善之罪，有而不知，當受闇塞之責。

translations.literal: As for senior clerks who have intent in serving the public but are not seen promoted and employed; there are greedy, covetous, filthy, turbid ones who by wealth and power secure themselves—if there is failure to raise them, ought receive the crime of intentional release and concealing the good; if there is having but not knowing, ought receive the blame of dark obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Where a worthy magistrate is passed over for promotion, or a corrupt one buys safety with gold and influence, any governor who fails to report him shall be guilty of shielding evil; one who truly did not know still bears the fault of blind negligence.

sentences.zh: 各明愼奉行。

translations.literal: Each clearly and carefully carry out and practice.
translations.idiomatic: Let every man carry this out with care."

sentences.zh: 」劉聰死，其子粲嗣偽位。

translations.literal: " Liu Cong died; his son Can succeeded the false position.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong died, and his son Liu Can succeeded to the usurper's throne.

sentences.zh: 八月，冀、徐、青三州蝗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Ji, Xu, and Qing three states had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month locusts swarmed Ji, Xu, and Qing provinces.

sentences.zh: 靳准弑劉粲，自號漢王。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun assassinated Liu Can; himself styled King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun murdered Liu Can and proclaimed himself king of Han.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸未，加廣州刺史陶侃平南將軍。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, guiwei, he added Inspector of Guangzhou Tao Kan as General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the tenth month Tao Kan, governor of Guangzhou, was additionally named general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 劉曜僭卽皇帝位于赤壁。

translations.literal: Liu Yao usurpingly ascended the emperor's position at Red Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao unlawfully declared himself emperor at Chibi.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月丁卯，崇陽陵毀，帝素服哭三日；

translations.literal: Second year, spring first month, dingmao, Chongyang Mausoleum was destroyed; the emperor in plain clothes wept three days;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year, on dingmao, the Chongyang imperial tomb collapsed; the emperor wore mourning white and wept three days;

sentences.zh: 使冠軍將軍梁堪、守太常馬龜等修復山陵。

translations.literal: he sent General Who Takes the Championship Liang Kan, Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies Ma Gui and others to repair and restore the mountain mausolea.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Liang Kan, general who takes the championship, Ma Gui, acting grand master of ceremonies, and others to repair the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 迎梓宮於平陽，不克而還。

translations.literal: Welcoming the catalpa palace at Pingyang, was not able and returned.
translations.idiomatic: An expedition to fetch the late emperor's coffin from Pingyang failed, and the party turned back.

sentences.zh: 二月，太山太守徐龕斬周撫，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the second month, Taishan Administrator Xu Kan beheaded Zhou Fu, transmitted the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Xu Kan, governor of Taishan, executed Zhou Fu and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，龍驤將軍陳川以浚儀叛，降于石勒。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, General of Dragon Soaring Chen Chuan with Junyi rebelled, surrendered to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chen Chuan, the dragon-soaring general, rebelled from Junyi and went over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 太山太守徐龕以郡叛，自號兗州刺史，寇濟岱。

translations.literal: Taishan Administrator Xu Kan with the commandery rebelled, self-styled Inspector of Yanzhou, raided Ji and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kan of Taishan then rose with his whole commandery, styled himself governor of Yanzhou, and raided the lands about Ji and Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史陳安叛，降于劉曜。

translations.literal: Inspector of Qinzhou Chen An rebelled, surrendered to Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An, governor of Qinzhou, mutinied and submitted to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 五月癸丑，太陽陵毀，帝素服哭三日。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on guichou, Taiyang Mausoleum was destroyed; the emperor in plain clothes wept three days.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the fifth month the Taiyang mausoleum fell in; again the emperor donned mourning white and wept three days.

sentences.zh: 徐楊及江西諸郡蝗。

translations.literal: Xu, Yang, and Jiangxi various commanderies had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged Xu, Yang, and the commanderies west of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 吳郡大饑。

translations.literal: Wu commandery had great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Great famine struck Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 平北將軍祖逖及石勒將石季龍戰于浚儀，王師敗績。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the North Zu Ti and Shi Le's general Shi Jilong battled at Junyi; the royal army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti, general who pacifies the north, met Shi Hu near Junyi; the imperial army suffered a sharp defeat.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔曰：「天下凋弊，加以災荒，百姓困窮，國用並匱，吳郡饑人死者百數。

translations.literal: On renxu an edict said: "The realm is withered and exhausted, added to disaster and famine; the hundred surnames are trapped in poverty; state use together is depleted; Wu commandery starving people dead number in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day he proclaimed: "The empire is worn thin and famine stalks the land; the people are desperate and the treasury empty; in Wu commandery alone hundreds have starved.

sentences.zh: 天生蒸黎而樹之以君，選建明哲以左右之，當深思以救其弊。

translations.literal: Heaven produced the steam-black masses and established for them a lord, selecting and establishing wise clarity to left and right them; ought deeply think thereby to save its harms.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven bred the people and set a ruler over them, choosing wise helpers at his side; we must think deeply how to cure these ills.

sentences.zh: 昔吳起爲楚悼王明法審令，捐不急之官，除廢公族疏遠，以附益將士，而國富兵強。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu Qi for King Dao of Chu clarified laws and examined orders, cast away not-urgent officials, removed and abolished ducal kin distant, thereby to attach and benefit generals and soldiers, and the state was rich and army strong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Qi served King Dao of Chu he tightened the laws, cut useless offices, stripped distant cadet branches of their stipends to feed the army, and so made Chu rich and its soldiers strong.

sentences.zh: 況今日之弊，百姓凋困邪！

translations.literal: How much more today's harms, the hundred surnames withered and trapped!
translations.idiomatic: How much more today, when the people are on their last breath!

sentences.zh: 且當去非急之務，非軍士所須者皆省之。

translations.literal: Moreover ought remove not-urgent tasks; what is not what army soldiers require, all reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: Cut every task that is not urgent and strike every expense the troops do not need."

sentences.zh: 」甲子，梁州刺史訪及杜曾戰于武當，斬之，禽第五猗。

translations.literal: " On jiazi, Inspector of Liangzhou Fang and Du Zeng battled at Wudang, beheaded him, captured Diwu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " On the jiazi day Zhou Fang, governor of Liangzhou, met Du Zeng at Wudang, slew him, and took Diwu Yi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 六月丙子，加周訪安南將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on bingzi he added Zhou Fang as General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day in the sixth month Zhou Fang was additionally named general who guards the south.

sentences.zh: 罷御府及諸郡丞，置博士員五人。

translations.literal: He abolished the imperial wardrobe office and the various commandery assistants; he established erudite posts, five persons.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the palace wardrobe office and the assistant posts in the commanderies and set five doctoral chairs at court.

sentences.zh: 己亥，加太常賀循開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On jihai he added Grand Master of Ceremonies He Xun Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day He Xun, grand master of ceremonies, was granted an independent headquarters with honors equal to the three highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙丑，太常賀循卒。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, yichou, Grand Master of Ceremonies He Xun died.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun, grand master of ceremonies, died on the yichou day in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 八月，肅愼獻楛矢石砮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Sushen presented ku arrows and stone arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month envoys from Sushen brought tribute of mulberry arrows and flint arrowheads.

sentences.zh: 徐龕寇東莞，遣太子左衛率羊鑒行征虜將軍，統徐州刺史蔡豹討之。

translations.literal: Xu Kan raided Dongguan; he dispatched the heir apparent's left guard leader Yang Jian to act as General Who Captures the Foe, commanding Xuzhou Inspector Cai Bao to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Kan raided Dongguan, the emperor sent Yang Jian, leader of the crown prince's left guard, as acting general who captures the foe, with Cai Bao, governor of Xuzhou, under his command to crush the rising.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，平北將軍祖逖使督護陳超襲石勒將桃豹，超敗，沒於陣。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, General Who Pacifies the North Zu Ti sent Army Supervisor Chen Chao to raid Shi Le's general Tao Bao; Chao was defeated and perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zu Ti ordered Chen Chao to strike Shi Le's general Tao Bao; Chen Chao was beaten and killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊寅，石勒僭卽王位，國號趙。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month on wuyin Shi Le usurpingly ascended the king's position; the state's title was Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the eleventh month Shi Le unlawfully took the title of king and named his state Zhao.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙亥，大赦，詔百官各上封事，幷省衆役。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month on yihai, great amnesty; he ordered the hundred officials each to submit sealed memorials and together reduce the multitude of corvées.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the twelfth month he proclaimed a general amnesty, called for sealed advice from every ministry, and ordered cuts to public labor.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑慕容廆襲遼東，東夷校尉、平州刺史崔毖奔高句驪。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Murong Hui raided Liaodong; Colonel of the Eastern Yi, Inspector of Pingzhou Cui Bi fled to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hui of the Xianbei struck Liaodong; Cui Bi, colonel of the eastern Yi and governor of Pingzhou, fled to Koguryŏ.

sentences.zh: 是歲，南陽王保稱晉王于祁山。

translations.literal: That year the Prince of Nanyang, Bao, styled himself Jin Prince at Qishan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sima Bao, prince of Nanyang, proclaimed himself Jin prince at Qishan.

sentences.zh: 三吳大饑。

translations.literal: The Three Wu had great famine.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the Three Wu region.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丁酉朔，晉王保爲劉曜所逼，遷于桑城。

translations.literal: Third year, spring first month, dingyou new moon, Jin Prince Bao was pressed by Liu Yao and moved to Sangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, on the new-moon day dingyou, Sima Bao, the Jin prince, was driven by Liu Yao to withdraw to Sangcheng.

sentences.zh: 二月辛未，石勒將石季龍寇猒次，平北將軍、冀州刺史邵續擊之，續敗，沒於陣。

translations.literal: In the second month on xinwei Shi Le's general Shi Jilong raided Yanci; General Who Pacifies the North, Jizhou Inspector Shao Xu struck him; Xu was defeated and perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the second month Shi Hu attacked Yanci; Shao Xu, the general who pacifies the north and governor of Jizhou, marched to meet him but was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 三月，慕容廆奉送玉璽三紐。

translations.literal: In the third month Murong Hui respectfully presented three jade seals with cords.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Murong Hui sent three imperial jade seals as tribute.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以尚書周顗爲尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month he appointed Secretary Zhou Yi as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Zhou Yi was promoted from secretary to vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬辰，枉矢流于翼軫。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, renchen, a crooked arrow meteor streamed through Yi and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the fourth month a "crooked-arrow" comet streaked across the lodges of Yi and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 五月丙寅，孝懷帝太子詮遇害于平陽，帝三日哭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on bingyin, Emperor Huai's heir apparent Quan met harm at Pingyang; the emperor wept three days.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the fifth month Sima Quan, the late Emperor Huai's crown prince, was murdered at Pingyang; the court kept three days of mourning.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，地震。

translations.literal: On gengyin there was an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: The earth shook on the gengyin day.

sentences.zh: 是月，晉王保爲其將張春所害。

translations.literal: That month Jin Prince Bao was killed by his general Zhang Chun.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Sima Bao, the Jin prince, was murdered by his general Zhang Chun.

sentences.zh: 劉曜使陳安攻春，滅之，安因叛曜。

translations.literal: Liu Yao sent Chen An to attack Chun, destroyed him; An thereupon rebelled against Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Chen An against Zhang Chun, destroyed his force, and then Chen An turned on Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 石勒將徐龕帥衆來降。

translations.literal: Shi Le's general Xu Kan led the multitude to come surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kan, a general under Shi Le, brought his army over to the Jin side.

sentences.zh: 六月，大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month there was great flood.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth month brought severe flooding.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，盜殺西中郎將、護羌校尉、涼州刺史、西平公張寔，寔弟茂嗣，領平西將軍、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingyou bandits killed General of the Western Center, Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, Inspector of Liangzhou, Duke of Xiping Zhang Shi; Shi's younger brother Mao succeeded, acting as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day assassins murdered Zhang Shi—general of the western center, Qiang commandant, governor of Liangzhou, and duke of Xiping. His brother Zhang Mao succeeded him as acting general who pacifies the west and governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁亥，詔曰：「先公武王、先考恭王臨君琅邪四十餘年，惠澤加于百姓，遺愛結于人情。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, dinghai, an edict said: "Former Duke Wu Wang, former deceased Duke Gong Wang faced and lorded Langye forty-odd years; favor and moisture were added to the hundred surnames; leftover love knotted in human feelings.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the seventh month an edict declared: "My grandfather King Wu and my late father King Gong ruled Langye for more than forty years; their kindness touched every household and their memory still binds the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 朕應天符，創基江表，兆庶宅心，繈負子來。

translations.literal: I have answered Heaven's tallies, founded the base south of the river; the trillion commoners lodge their hearts; swaddled-burdened children come.
translations.idiomatic: I have answered Heaven's omens and laid the foundations south of the Yangzi; the millions look to me as their home, and families flock to me as to a father.

sentences.zh: 琅邪國人在此者近有千戶，今立爲懷德縣，統丹陽郡。

translations.literal: Langye state people who are here are nearly a thousand households; now establish them as Huaide County, subordinate to Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly a thousand households of our old Langye subjects now live here; I create for them Huaide county under the administration of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖以沛爲湯沐邑，光武亦復南頓，優復之科一依漢氏故事。

translations.literal: Formerly Han Gaozu took Pei as bath-fief; Guangwu likewise again Nandun; the grades of favor and remission one by one follow Han house precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu once made his home county of Pei a ritual fief, and Guangwu did the same for Nandun; the tax relief I grant shall follow those Han precedents in every detail."

sentences.zh: 」祖逖部將衛策大破石勒別軍於汴水。

translations.literal: " Zu Ti's division general Wei Ce greatly defeated Shi Le's separate army at Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: " Meanwhile Zu Ti's officer Wei Ce shattered a detached column of Shi Le's army on the Bian River.

sentences.zh: 加逖爲鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: He added Ti as General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti was promoted to general who guards the west.

sentences.zh: 八月戊午，尊敬王后虞氏爲敬皇后。

translations.literal: In the eighth month on wuwu he honored the late queen, Lady Yu, as Empress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the eighth month Lady Yu, the late queen, was posthumously honored as Empress Jing.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，遷神主于太廟。

translations.literal: On xinyou he moved the spirit tablets to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day the imperial spirit tablets were carried into the grand ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 辛未，梁州刺史、安南將軍周訪卒。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Inspector of Liangzhou, General Who Guards the South Zhou Fang died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang, governor of Liangzhou and general who guards the south, died on the xinwei day.

sentences.zh: 皇太子釋尊于太學。

translations.literal: The imperial heir apparent released the cap at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince performed the capping rite at the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 以湘州刺史甘卓爲安南將軍、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Xiangzhou Inspector Gan Zhuo as General Who Guards the South, Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo was transferred from Xiangzhou to be general who guards the south and governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，徐龕又叛，降于石勒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Xu Kan again rebelled, surrendered to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Xu Kan rebelled again and went over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙辰，徐州刺史蔡豹以畏愞伏誅。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month on bingchen, Xuzhou Inspector Cai Bao because of cowardice and timidity submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen in the tenth month Cai Bao, governor of Xuzhou, was executed for cowardice in the field.

sentences.zh: 王敦殺武陵內史向碩。

translations.literal: Wang Dun killed Wuling Administrator Xiang Shuo.
