translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had Xiang Shuo, the administrator of Wuling, put to death.

sentences.zh: 四年春二月，徐龕又帥衆來降。

translations.literal: Fourth year, spring second month, Xu Kan again led the multitude to come surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Xu Kan once more brought his troops in to surrender.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑末波奉送皇帝信璽。

translations.literal: The Xianbei Mobo respectfully presented the emperor's credence seal.
translations.idiomatic: Mobo of the Xianbei sent the emperor's bronze credence seal.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，告於太廟，乃受之。

translations.literal: On gengxu he announced at the Grand Temple, then received it.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day he reported to the grand temple and formally received the seal.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，日鬭。

translations.literal: On guihai the suns fought.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day the sun showed the "eclipse battle" omen—two disks contending in the sky.

sentences.zh: 三月，置《周易》、《儀禮》、《公羊》博士。

translations.literal: In the third month he established Zhou Yi, Yili, Gongyang erudites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he created doctoral chairs for the Zhou Changes, the Book of Etiquette and Rites, and the Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以平東將軍曹嶷爲安東將軍。

translations.literal: On guiyou he appointed General Who Pacifies the East Cao Yi as General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day Cao Yi was promoted from general who pacifies the east to general who guards the east.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛亥，帝親覽庶獄。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, xinhai, the emperor personally examined the multitude of prisons.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the fourth month the emperor personally reviewed criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 石勒攻猒次，陷之。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked Yanci, captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le stormed Yanci and took the city.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍、幽州刺史段匹磾沒于勒。

translations.literal: General Who Garrisons the Army, Youzhou Inspector Duan Pidi was lost to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi, the general who garrisons the army and governor of Youzhou, fell into Shi Le's hands.

sentences.zh: 五月，旱。

translations.literal: In the fifth month there was drought.
translations.idiomatic: Drought gripped the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔曰：「昔漢二祖及魏武皆免良人，武帝時，涼州覆敗，諸爲奴婢亦皆復籍，此累代成規也。

translations.literal: On gengshen an edict said: "Formerly Han's two founders and Wei Wu all freed good people; at Emperor Wu's time, Liangzhou overturned and defeated, those who were slaves and maids all also restored registers; this is successive generations' settled rule.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day he decreed: "The two founders of Han and Cao Cao of Wei both freed commoners pressed into servitude; under Emperor Wu, when Liangzhou collapsed, every bondsman was returned to free status. Such relief has been the settled practice of many reigns.

sentences.zh: 其免中州良人遭難爲揚州諸郡僮客者，以備征役。」

translations.literal: As for freeing central province good people who met disaster and became Yangzhou various commanderies retainers and clients, thereby to prepare for conscript labor."
translations.idiomatic: Let every freeborn northerner who, in the turmoil, became a tenant or bondsman in Yangzhou be restored to commoner status so he may again bear arms for the state."

sentences.zh: 秋七月，大水。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, there was great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month catastrophic floods struck.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以尚書戴若思爲征西將軍、都督司兗豫幷冀雍六州諸軍事、司州刺史，鎮合肥；

translations.literal: On jiaxu he appointed Secretary Dai Ruosi as General Who Conquers the West, Area Commander-in-Chief of Si, Yan, Yu, Bing, Ji, Yong six states' military affairs, Inspector of Sizhou, garrisoning Hefei;
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day Dai Ruosi was named general who conquers the west, area commander for six northern provinces, and governor of Sizhou, with headquarters at Hefei;

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹劉隗爲鎮北將軍、都督青徐幽平四州諸軍事、青州刺史，鎮淮陰。

translations.literal: Danyang Intendant Liu Wei was made General Who Guards the North, Area Commander-in-Chief of Qing, Xu, You, Ping four states' military affairs, Inspector of Qingzhou, garrisoning Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: while Liu Wei, the intendant of Danyang, became general who guards the north, commander for Qing, Xu, You, and Ping, governor of Qingzhou, and encamped at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 壬千，以驃騎將軍王導爲司空。

translations.literal: On renqian he appointed General of Agile Cavalry Wang Dao as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the renqian day Wang Dao was moved from general of agile cavalry to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 八月，常山崩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Mount Chang collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Mount Chang suffered a landslide.

sentences.zh: 九月壬寅，鎮西將軍、豫州刺史祖逖卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month on renyin, General Who Guards the West, Yuzhou Inspector Zu Ti died.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti, the general who guards the west and governor of Yuzhou, died on the renyin day in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬午，以逖弟侍中約爲平西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month on renwu he appointed Ti's younger brother, Palace Attendant Yue, as General Who Pacifies the West, Yuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the tenth month Zu Yue, the palace attendant and younger brother of Zu Ti, succeeded him as general who pacifies the west and governor of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以慕容廆爲持節、都督幽平二州東夷諸軍事、平州牧，封遼東郡公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he appointed Murong Hui as Bearer of the Scepter, Area Commander-in-Chief of You and Ping two states' Eastern Yi military affairs, Governor of Pingzhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Liaodong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Hui received the imperial baton, command over the eastern Yi of You and Ping, the governorship of Pingzhou, and the title of duke of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年正月乙卯，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: Yongchang first year, first month on yimao, great amnesty, changed era name.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the first month of the first year of Yongchang he proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the new reign title.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，大將軍王敦舉兵於武昌，以誅劉隗爲名，龍驤將軍沈充帥衆應之。

translations.literal: On wuchen Grand General Wang Dun raised troops at Wuchang, taking executing Liu Wei as pretext; General of Dragon Soaring Shen Chong led the multitude to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day Grand General Wang Dun rose in arms at Wuchang on the pretext of punishing Liu Wei, while Shen Chong, the dragon-soaring general, brought his army to join him.

sentences.zh: 三月，徵征西將軍戴若思、鎮北將軍劉隗還衛京都。

translations.literal: In the third month he summoned General Who Conquers the West Dai Ruosi, General Who Guards the North Liu Wei to return and guard the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Dai Ruosi and Liu Wei were recalled from the front to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 以司空王導爲前鋒大都督，以戴若思爲驃騎將軍，丹陽諸郡皆加軍號。

translations.literal: He appointed Minister of Works Wang Dao as Vanguard Grand Area Commander-in-Chief; appointed Dai Ruosi as General of Agile Cavalry; Danyang various commanderies all were added military titles.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao was named commander of the vanguard, Dai Ruosi became general of agile cavalry, and every Danyang county received a military designation.

sentences.zh: 加僕射周顗尚書左僕射，領軍王邃尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He added Vice Director Zhou Yi as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat; Army Commandant Wang Sui as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi was promoted to left vice director of the secretariat and Wang Sui, the army commandant, to right vice director.

sentences.zh: 以太子右衛率周筵行冠軍將軍，統兵三千討沈充。

translations.literal: He appointed the heir apparent's right guard leader Zhou Yan to act as General Who Takes the Championship, commanding three thousand troops to campaign against Shen Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yan, leader of the crown prince's right guard, was given the brevet rank of general who takes the championship and three thousand men to move against Shen Chong.

sentences.zh: 甲午，封皇子昱爲琅邪王。

translations.literal: On jiawu he enfeoffed the imperial son Yu as Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day the emperor's son Sima Yu was invested as prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 劉隗軍于金城，右將軍周札守石頭，帝親被甲徇六師於郊外。

translations.literal: Liu Wei encamped at Jincheng; General of the Right Zhou Zha guarded Stone Rampart; the emperor personally donned armor and inspected the six armies beyond the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei took position at Jincheng, Zhou Zha, general of the right, held Stone City, and the emperor buckled on his armor and rode through the six hosts outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 遣平南將軍陶侃領江州，安南將軍甘卓領荊州，各帥所統以躡敦後。

translations.literal: He dispatched General Who Pacifies the South Tao Kan to take Jiangzhou, General Who Guards the South Gan Zhuo to take Jingzhou, each leading what they commanded to follow on Dun's rear.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Tao Kan, the general who pacifies the south, to take charge of Jiangzhou and Gan Zhuo, the general who guards the south, of Jingzhou, each marching to fall on Wang Dun from behind.

sentences.zh: 四月，敦前鋒攻石頭，周札開城門應之，奮威將軍侯禮死之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Dun's vanguard attacked Stone Rampart; Zhou Zha opened the city gate to respond to them; General Who Rouses Might Hou Li died for it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wang Dun's van stormed Stone City; Zhou Zha opened the gates to him, and Hou Li, the general who rouses might, died defending the wall.

sentences.zh: 敦據石頭，戴若思、劉隗帥衆攻之，王導、周顗、郭逸、虞潭等三道出戰，六軍敗績。

translations.literal: Dun occupied Stone Rampart; Dai Ruosi, Liu Wei led the multitude to attack him; Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Guo Yi, Yu Tan and others three routes went out to battle; the six armies were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun seized Stone City. Dai Ruosi and Liu Wei attacked him while Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Guo Yi, and Yu Tan sallied by three roads, but the imperial army was routed.

sentences.zh: 尚書令刁協奔於江乘，爲賊所害。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Diao Xie fled to Jiangcheng; was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie, director of the secretariat, fled toward Jiangcheng and was cut down by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍劉隗奔于石勒。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the North Liu Wei fled to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei, the general who guards the north, fled north and threw in his lot with Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使謂敦曰：「公若不忘本朝，於此息兵，則天下尚可共安也。

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to say to Dun: "If the duke does not forget this court, here cease arms, then the realm still can be together at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word to Wang Dun: "If you still care for the house of Jin and halt your armies here, the realm may yet know peace again.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，騰當歸於琅邪，以避賢路。

translations.literal: If it is not so, Teng shall return to Langye, thereby to yield the worthy road.
translations.idiomatic: If not, I shall retire to my old fief of Langye and leave the field to worthier men."

sentences.zh: 」辛未，大赦。

translations.literal: " On xinwei, great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: " On the xinwei day he proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 敦乃自爲丞相、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，封武昌郡公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Dun thereupon himself became chancellor, Area Commander-in-Chief of all armies within and without, Recorder of Secretariat Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Wuchang commandery, fief ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun then named himself chancellor, commander of all forces, and recorder of the secretariat, and took the title of duke of Wuchang with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 丙子，驃騎將軍、秣陵侯戴若思，尚書左僕射、護軍將軍、武城侯周顗爲敦所害。

translations.literal: On bingzi, General of Agile Cavalry, Marquis of Moling Dai Ruosi, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, General Who Guards the Army, Marquis of Wucheng Zhou Yi were killed by Dun.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day Wang Dun executed Dai Ruosi, general of agile cavalry and marquis of Moling, and Zhou Yi, left vice director of the secretariat, general who guards the army, and marquis of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 敦將沈充陷吳國，魏乂陷湘州，吳國內史張茂，湘州刺史、譙王承並遇害。

translations.literal: Dun's general Shen Chong captured Wu state; Wei Yi captured Xiangzhou; Wu Administrator Zhang Mao, Xiangzhou Inspector, Prince of Qiao Cheng together met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong, Wang Dun's officer, overran Wu commandery; Wei Yi took Hunan; Zhang Mao, the administrator of Wu, and Sima Cheng, prince of Qiao and governor of Xiangzhou, were both killed.

sentences.zh: 五月壬申，敦乙太保、西陽王羕爲太宰，加司空王導尚書令。

translations.literal: In the fifth month on renshen Dun appointed Grand Guardian, Prince of Xiyang Yang as Grand Preceptor; added Minister of Works Wang Dao as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the fifth month Wang Dun named Sima Yang, prince of Xiyang and grand guardian, grand preceptor, and made Wang Dao, the minister of works, director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，鎮南大將軍甘卓爲襄陽太守周慮所害。

translations.literal: On yihai Grand General Who Guards the South Gan Zhuo was killed by Xiangyang Administrator Zhou Lu.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day Gan Zhuo, the grand general who guards the south, was murdered by Zhou Lu, the governor of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 蜀賊張龍寇巴東，建平太守柳純擊走之。

translations.literal: Shu bandit Zhang Long raided Badong; Jianping Administrator Liu Chun struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu rebel Zhang Long raided Badong but was driven off by Liu Chun, governor of Jianping.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣騎寇河南。

translations.literal: Shi Le dispatched cavalry to raid south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent horsemen to raid the lands south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 六月，旱。

translations.literal: In the sixth month there was drought.
translations.idiomatic: Drought returned in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，王敦自加兗州刺史郗鑒爲安北將軍。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Wang Dun himself added Yanzhou Inspector Xi Jian as General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wang Dun on his own authority promoted Xi Jian, the governor of Yanzhou, to general who guards the north.

sentences.zh: 石勒將石季龍攻陷太山，執守將徐龕。

translations.literal: Shi Le's general Shi Jilong attacked and captured Taishan, seized defending general Xu Kan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, serving under Shi Le, took Taishan and captured the defender Xu Kan.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史郗鑒自鄒山退守合肥。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Xi Jian from Zou Mountain retreated to guard Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian, governor of Yanzhou, fell back from Zou Mountain to hold Hefei.

sentences.zh: 八月，敦以其見含爲衛將軍，自領寧、益二州都督。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Dun because his elder brother Han was Guards General, himself took concurrent Ning and Yi two provinces' Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wang Dun appointed his elder brother Wang Han guards-general and added the Ning and Yi military commands to his own portfolio.

sentences.zh: 琅邪太守孫默叛，降于石勒。

translations.literal: Langye Administrator Sun Mo rebelled, surrendered to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mo, the governor of Langye, rebelled and went over to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，大疫，死者十二三。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, great pestilence; of those stricken, two or three in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month a great plague swept the capital; as many as two or three in every ten of the sick perished.

sentences.zh: 己丑，都督荊梁二州諸軍事、平南將軍、荊州刺史、武陵侯王暠卒。

translations.literal: On jichou, Area Commander-in-Chief of Jing and Liang two states' military affairs, General Who Pacifies the South, Jingzhou Inspector, Marquis of Wuling Wang Hao died.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day Wang Hao died—he had commanded the armies of Jing and Liang, held the posts of general who pacifies the south and governor of Jingzhou, and bore the title marquis of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以下邳內史王邃爲征北將軍、都督青徐幽平四州諸軍事，鎮淮陰。

translations.literal: On xinmao he appointed Xiapi Administrator Wang Sui as General Who Conquers the North, Area Commander-in-Chief of Qing, Xu, You, Ping four states' military affairs, garrisoning Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day Wang Sui, the administrator of Xiapi, was named general who conquers the north, commander of Qing, Xu, You, and Ping, and stationed at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 新昌太守梁碩起兵反。

translations.literal: Xinchang Administrator Liang Shuo raised troops and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo, governor of Xinchang, rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 京師大霧，黑氣蔽天，日月無光。

translations.literal: The capital had great fog; black vapor covered the sky; sun and moon had no light.
translations.idiomatic: A heavy fog hung over the capital, black vapors veiled the sky, and neither sun nor moon could be seen.

sentences.zh: 石勒攻陷襄城、城父，遂圍譙，破祖約別軍，約退據壽春。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked and captured Xiangcheng, Chengfu; thereupon besieged Qiao, broke Zu Yue's separate army; Yue retreated to occupy Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le stormed Xiangcheng and Chengfu, then surrounded Qiao, destroyed a detached force under Zu Yue, and drove Zu Yue back to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以司徒荀組爲太尉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he appointed Minister of Education Xun Zu as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xun Zu was moved from minister of education to grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 己酉，太尉荀組薨。

translations.literal: On jiyou Grand Commandant Xun Zu died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Xun Zu died on the jiyou day.

sentences.zh: 罷司徒，幷丞相。

translations.literal: He abolished Minister of Education, merged with chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The office of minister of education was abolished and its duties folded into the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 閏月己丑，帝崩于內殿，時年四十七，葬建平陵，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: Intercalary month jichou, the emperor collapsed in the inner hall; at the time age forty-seven; buried at Jianping Mausoleum; temple name Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the intercalary month he died in the inner palace at forty-seven. He lies in the Jianping mausoleum and bears the temple name Zhongzong.

sentences.zh: 帝性簡儉沖素，容納直言，虛己待物。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was simple, frugal, humble, plain; he contained and admitted straight speech; he emptied himself to treat things.
translations.idiomatic: He was frugal, modest, and plain in habit, welcomed blunt counsel, and met the world with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 初鎮江東，頗以酒廢事，王導深以爲言，帝命酌，引觴覆之，於此遂絕。

translations.literal: When first garrisoning east of the river, rather by wine neglected affairs; Wang Dao deeply took it as a topic; the emperor ordered pour wine, drew the cup and overturned it; from this then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his tenure south of the Yangzi he sometimes neglected duty for wine until Wang Dao remonstrated sharply; the emperor called for a cup, raised it, and dashed it to the floor—after that he touched no more drink.

sentences.zh: 有司嘗奏太極殿廣室施絳帳，帝曰：「漢文集上書皁囊爲帷。

translations.literal: The responsible officials once memorialized to hang crimson curtains in the broad chamber of the Grand Ultimate Hall; the emperor said: "The Han court used the black document pouches in which memorials arrived as its model for curtains.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministry asked to hang crimson curtains in the great hall of the Grand Ultimate, he replied, "The Han emperors took the plain black silk bags that held memorials as their pattern for hangings.

sentences.zh: 」遂令冬施青布，夏施青綀帷帳。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ordered in winter hang blue cloth, in summer hang blue pongee curtains and tents.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore had plain blue cloth hung in winter and light blue gauze curtains in summer."

sentences.zh: 將拜貴人，有司請市雀釵，帝以煩費不許。

translations.literal: When about to invest a noble lady, the responsible officials requested to buy sparrow hairpins; the emperor because troublesome expense did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: When a consort was to be elevated, the ministry asked to purchase jeweled sparrow pins; he refused, calling the expense needless.

sentences.zh: 所幸鄭夫人衣無文彩。

translations.literal: The favored Lady Zheng's clothes had no patterned colors.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite, Lady Zheng, wore plain cloth without brocade.

sentences.zh: 從母弟王廙爲母立屋過制，流涕止之。

translations.literal: Maternal cousin Wang Yi for his mother built a house exceeding regulations; weeping tears he stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin Wang Yi built his mother a house above his rank, the emperor wept until the project was halted.

sentences.zh: 然晉室遘紛，皇輿播越，天命未改，人謀叶贊。

translations.literal: Yet the Jin house met disorder, the imperial chariot was cast about; Heaven's mandate was not yet changed; men's plans harmonized in support.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the house of Jin was torn by rebellion, the throne driven into exile; Heaven had not withdrawn its mandate, and human counsel still rallied to the cause.

sentences.zh: 元戎屢動，不出江畿，經略區區，僅全吳楚。

translations.literal: The great army repeatedly moved, did not go beyond the Yangzi's bounds; planning and strategy were paltry, barely preserving Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Though armies marched again and again, they never crossed the Yangzi frontier; his strategic reach was narrow, and he barely held Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 終于下陵上辱，憂憤告謝。

translations.literal: In the end the lower encroached on the higher in humiliation; in grief and anger he announced resignation.
translations.idiomatic: In the end inferiors shamed their sovereign; he died broken with grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 恭儉之德雖充，雄武之量不足。

translations.literal: Though the virtue of respect and frugality was full, the capacity for heroic martiality was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He had modesty and thrift in abundance, but lacked the stature of a conqueror.

sentences.zh: 始秦時望氣者云「五百年後金陵有天子氣」，故始皇東遊以厭之，改其地曰秣陵，塹北山以絕其勢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qin, a qi-watcher said, "Five hundred years hence Jinling will have Son of Heaven qi"; therefore the First Emperor toured east to suppress it, changed its place's name to Moling, trenched the northern hill to cut off its force.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner said that in five hundred years Jinling would bear imperial aura, so the First Emperor toured the east to break the omen, renamed the place Moling, and cut a trench through the northern hills to sever its geomantic power. A prophecy ran, "Five hundred years hence Jinling will have the aura of a Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 及孫權之稱號。

translations.literal: When it came to Sun Quan's assuming the title.
translations.idiomatic: The moment arrived when Sun Quan assumed the royal title.

sentences.zh: 自謂當之。

translations.literal: He himself thought he matched it.
translations.idiomatic: He believed he was the man the prophecy meant.

sentences.zh: 孫盛以爲始皇逮于孫氏四百三十七載，考其曆數，猶爲未及；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng thought that from the First Emperor to reaching the Sun clan was four hundred thirty-seven years; examining its reckoned succession, still was not yet reached;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng observed that only 437 years lay between the First Emperor and the house of Sun—by the reckoning of cycles the span had not yet been fulfilled;

sentences.zh: 元帝之渡江也，乃五百二十六年，眞人之應在于此矣。

translations.literal: when Yuan Emperor crossed the river, it was then five hundred twenty-six years; the true man's response lay in this.
translations.idiomatic: but when Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi, 526 years had passed—the true bearer of the mandate was clearly he.

sentences.zh: 咸寧初，風吹太社樹折，社中有青氣，占者以爲東莞有帝者之祥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning, wind blew the Grand Altar of Soil's tree broken; in the altar there was green vapor; diviners thought Dongguan had an emperor's auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianning a gale snapped the tree at the grand soil altar and a green mist rose from the mound; diviners read it as a sign that Dongguan would breed a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 由是徙封東莞王於琅邪，卽武王也。

translations.literal: Thereby the enfeoffed Prince of Dongguan was moved to Langye—this was King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Dongguan was therefore transferred to Langye—he who became King Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 及吳之亡，王濬實先至建鄴，而皓之降款，遠歸璽於琅邪。

translations.literal: When it came to Wu's perishing, Wang Jun in truth first arrived at Jianye; but Hao's surrendering sincerity, from afar returned the seal to Langye.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu fell Wang Jun was first into Jianye, yet Sun Hao's surrender sent the imperial seal all the way back to Langye.

sentences.zh: 天意人事，又符中興之兆。

translations.literal: Heaven's intent and human affairs again matched the omen of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and history together pointed again to a second founding.

sentences.zh: 太安之際，童謠云：「五馬浮渡江，一馬化爲龍。

translations.literal: At the time of Tai'an, children's rhyme said: "Five horses float crossing the river; one horse transforms into a dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tai'an era a children's song ran: "Five horses float across the river; one becomes a dragon."

sentences.zh: 」及永嘉中，歲、鎮、熒惑、太白聚斗、牛之間，識者以爲吳越之地當興王者。

translations.literal: " Reaching Yongjia, Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, and Venus gathered between Dipper and Ox; those who understood thought the lands of Wu and Yue would raise a kingly man.
translations.idiomatic: " By Yongjia, Jupiter, Saturn, Mars, and Venus had massed between the lodges Dipper and Ox; wise men said a king would rise in the Wu–Yue region.

sentences.zh: 是歲，王室淪覆，帝與西陽、汝南、南頓、彭城五王獲濟，而帝竟登大位焉。

translations.literal: That year the royal house sank and was overturned; the emperor together with Xiyang, Runan, Nandun, Pengcheng five princes obtained rescue; yet the emperor in the end ascended the great position.
translations.idiomatic: That year the dynasty collapsed; he and the princes of Xiyang, Runan, Nandun, and Pengcheng were among the few who escaped across the river, and he alone climbed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，《玄石圖》有「牛繼馬後」，故宣帝深忌牛氏，遂爲二榼，共一口，以貯酒焉，帝先飲佳者，而以毒酒鴆其將牛金。

translations.literal: Formerly, in the Dark Stone Chart there was "the ox follows the horse"; therefore Emperor Xuan deeply dreaded the Niu clan; then made two flasks, sharing one mouth, to store wine therein; the emperor first drank the fine, but with poisoned wine zhenned his general Niu Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Dark Stone Chart once warned that "an ox would follow the horse"; Emperor Xuan therefore feared the Niu surname, set out paired flasks with a single spout, drank the good wine himself, and poisoned his general Niu Jin from the other.

sentences.zh: 而恭王妃夏侯氏竟通小吏牛氏而生元帝，亦有符云。

translations.literal: Yet King Gong's consort Lady Xiahou in the end connected with clerk Niu and bore Yuan Emperor; there was also a tally saying so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Princess Xiahou of Gong took up with a minor clerk surnamed Niu and bore Emperor Yuan—another omen fulfilled, men said.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：晉氏不虞，自中流外，五胡扛鼎，七廟隳尊，滔天方駕，則民懷其舊德者矣。

translations.literal: The historians say: The Jin clan did not foresee it; from midstream outward, the five Hu shouldered the tripod, the seven temples toppled their honor; flooding Heaven side by side—then the people cherished its old virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Jin could not guard against calamity from within; beyond the heartland the Five Hu seized the cauldron, the imperial shrines were cast down, and rebellion rose like a flood—so the people clung to the memory of better days.

sentences.zh: 昔光武以數郡加名，元皇以一州臨極，豈武宣餘化猶暢于琅邪，文景垂仁傳芳于南頓，所謂後乎天時，先諸人事者也。

translations.literal: Formerly Guangwu by several commanderies added fame; Yuan Huang by one province faced the extreme—was it that Wu and Xuan's remaining transformation still flowed at Langye, Wen and Jing's hanging benevolence transmitted fragrance at Nandun—what is called behind Heaven's timing, ahead of the multitude of human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu rose from a handful of commanderies, while Emperor Yuan ruled from a single province—perhaps the lingering virtue of Sima Yi and his sons still warmed Langye, and the kindness of Han Wendi and Jingdi still lingered at Nandun: fate came late, but human effort came first.

sentences.zh: 馳章獻號，高蓋成陰，星斗呈祥，金陵表慶。

translations.literal: Galloping memorials presented titles; high canopies became shade; stars and constellations showed auspice; Jinling displayed celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials flew in offering the throne, noble coaches crowded the roads like a forest, the stars showed blessing, and Jinling proclaimed good fortune.

sentences.zh: 陶士行擁三州之旅，郢外以安；

translations.literal: Tao Shixing embraced three provinces' hosts; outside Ying thereby was pacified;
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan held three provinces' troops and the country beyond Jing grew calm;

sentences.zh: 王茂弘爲分陝之計，江東可立。

translations.literal: Wang Maohong made the divided-Shaan plan; east of the river could be established.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao laid plans like the ancient "divided Shaan" partnership, and the lower Yangzi could stand as a realm.

sentences.zh: 或高旌未拂，而遐心斯偃，回首朝陽，仰希乾棟，帝猶六讓不居，七辭而不免也。

translations.literal: Perhaps high banners not yet waved, yet distant hearts thereby lay low; turning the head toward the morning sun, looking up hoping for the Qian ridgepole—yet the emperor still six times yielded not to dwell, seven times declined yet could not avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Before his banners had swept the north, distant hearts already bowed; all eyes turned to the rising sun and looked for a pillar of state—yet even after six refusals of the throne and seven pleas to be spared, he could not escape taking it.

sentences.zh: 布帳綀帷，詳刑簡化，抑揚前軌，光啓中興。

translations.literal: Cloth curtains and pongee hangings; detailed punishments, simplified transformation; suppressing and raising former tracks, broadly opening restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Plain curtains and gauze screens, careful justice and lean government—he trimmed the excesses of the past and lit the torch of the restoration.

sentences.zh: 古首私家不蓄甲兵，大臣不爲威福，王之常制，以訓股肱。

translations.literal: From of old it has been said: private families do not store armor and weapons; great ministers do not make awesomeness and fortune—this is the king's constant regulation, whereby to instruct thigh and arm.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that private houses must not hoard arms and that ministers must not wield arbitrary power—such is the king's standing rule for teaching his servants.

sentences.zh: 中宗失馭強臣，自亡齊斧，兩京胡羯，風埃相望。

translations.literal: Zhongzong lost control of strong ministers, himself lost the Qi axe; two capitals Hu and Jie, wind and dust face each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong failed to bridle mighty vassals and so lost the regal axe himself; the twin capitals fell to Hu and Jie, and dust of war stretched from plain to plain.

sentences.zh: 雖復《六月》之駕無聞，而《鴻雁》之歌方遠，享國無幾，哀哉！

translations.literal: Although again the "Sixth Month" chariot was unheard of, yet the "Wild Geese" song was still distant; enjoying the state not many—alas!
translations.idiomatic: He never heard the war-chariots of the "Sixth Month" ode, and the lament of "Wild Geese" still rang far off; his reign was brief—how pitiful!

sentences.zh: 明皇帝

translations.literal: Emperor Ming
translations.idiomatic: The annals turn to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 明皇帝諱紹，字道畿，元皇帝長子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's taboo name was Shao, courtesy name Daoji; he was Yuan Emperor's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, personal name Shao and courtesy name Daoji, was the eldest son of Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰哲，爲元帝所寵異。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and wise; by Yuan Emperor was favored as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed unusual wit, and his father singled him out for favor.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，嘗坐置膝前，屬長安使來，因問帝曰：「汝謂日與長安孰遠？

translations.literal: At age several years, once sitting placed before the knees, just when a Chang'an envoy came, thereby asked the emperor, saying: "You say the sun and Chang'an which is farther?
translations.idiomatic: When he was still small he sat on his father's knee as an envoy from Chang'an arrived, and Yuan asked him, "Which do you think lies farther away—the sun or Chang'an?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「長安近。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Chang'an is near.
translations.idiomatic: " "Chang'an is nearer."

sentences.zh: 不聞人從日邊來，居然可知也。

translations.literal: I do not hear of people coming from beside the sun; thus it can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Nobody says he has come from beside the sun, so the answer is plain."

sentences.zh: 」元帝異之。

translations.literal: " Yuan Emperor thought him strange.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan marveled at the boy.

sentences.zh: 明日，宴羣僚，又問之。

translations.literal: The next day, feasting the host of officials, again asked him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day at a banquet for his ministers he put the question again.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「日近。

translations.literal: He replied: "The sun is near.
translations.idiomatic: This time the child said, "The sun is nearer."

sentences.zh: 」元帝失色，曰：「何乃異間者之言乎？

translations.literal: Yuan Emperor lost color, saying, "How can this differ from what you said before?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blanched and said, "Why does that contradict the answer you gave yesterday?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「舉目則見日，不見長安。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Raising the eyes then sees the sun; does not see Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " "I lift my eyes and see the sun, but I do not see Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 」由是益奇之。

translations.literal: " From this all the more thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " From that day his father prized him the more.

sentences.zh: 建興初，拜東中郎將，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing he was appointed General of the Eastern Center and garrisoned Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianxing era he became general of the eastern center and took post at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 元帝爲晉王，立爲晉王太子。

translations.literal: When Yuan Emperor was Jin Prince, he was established as Jin Prince Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When his father held the title of Prince of Jin, he was named heir to that princedom.

sentences.zh: 及帝卽尊號，立爲皇太子。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the exalted title, he was established as imperial heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan took the imperial throne, he was created crown prince.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，有文武才略，欽賢愛客，雅好文辭。

translations.literal: His nature was utmost filial; he had civil and martial talent and strategy; he honored worthies and loved guests; he elegantly loved literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial, gifted in both civil and military affairs, delighted in worthy men and open house, and cultivated a love of letters.

sentences.zh: 當時名臣，自王導、庚亮、溫嶠、桓彝、阮放等，咸見親待。

translations.literal: The time's famous ministers, from Wang Dao, Geng Liang, Wen Qiao, Huan Yi, Ruan Fang and the like, all were seen close and treated.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ministers of the day—Wang Dao, Yu Liang, Wen Qiao, Huan Yi, Ruan Fang, and others—all enjoyed his intimate confidence.

sentences.zh: 嘗論聖人眞假之意，導等不能屈。

translations.literal: He once discussed the sages' true and false meaning; Dao and the others could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he debated the subtle question of true and false in the sage's teaching, and not even Wang Dao could get the better of him.

sentences.zh: 又習武藝，善撫將士。

translations.literal: Also he practiced martial arts; was good at soothing generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in arms and knew how to win the hearts of his troops.

sentences.zh: 於時東朝濟濟，遠近屬心焉。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern court was numerous; far and near attached their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern palace then stood full of talent, and men near and far pinned their hopes on him.

sentences.zh: 及王敦之亂，六軍敗績，帝欲帥將士決戰，升車將出，中庶子溫嶠固諫，抽劍斬鞅，乃止。

translations.literal: When it came to Wang Dun's rebellion, the six armies were defeated; the emperor wished to lead generals and soldiers to decisive battle, ascended the chariot about to go out; Palace Attendant Wen Qiao firmly remonstrated, drew sword and cut the chariot strap, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Dun's revolt the imperial army was routed; he wanted to lead a sortie in person and had stepped into his carriage when Wen Qiao, his attendant of the palace, barred the way, drew his sword, and severed the traces—only then did he give up.

sentences.zh: 敦素以帝神武明略，朝野之所欽信，欲誣以不孝而廢焉。

translations.literal: Dun always because the emperor was divinely martial and clearly strategized, what court and wilds admired and trusted, wished to slander him with unfiliality and abolish him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun knew the heir enjoyed a reputation for courage and clear judgment, trusted at court and in the country, so he plotted to brand him unfilial and depose him.

sentences.zh: 大會百官而問溫嶠曰：「皇太子以何德稱？

translations.literal: He greatly assembled the hundred officials and asked Wen Qiao, saying: "By what virtue does the imperial heir apparent deserve praise?
translations.idiomatic: At a full assembly of officials he demanded of Wen Qiao, "What merit earns the crown prince his name?"

sentences.zh: 」聲色俱厲，必欲使有言。

translations.literal: " Voice and color both severe; he was determined to make him have words.
translations.idiomatic: " His voice and face were fierce; he would force an answer.

sentences.zh: 嶠對曰：「鉤深致遠，蓋非淺局所量。

translations.literal: Qiao replied: "Hooking the deep and reaching the far—this is probably not what shallow confines can measure.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao answered, "To plumb the depths and see far ahead is beyond the measure of petty minds.

sentences.zh: 以禮觀之，可稱爲孝矣。

translations.literal: Viewing by the rites, he can be called filial."
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the rites, he may truly be called a filial son."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆以爲信然，敦謀遂止。

translations.literal: " The multitude all thought it trustworthy; Dun's plot then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembly accepted this, and Wang Dun dropped his scheme.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年閏月己丑，元帝崩。

translations.literal: Yongchang first year, intercalary month jichou, Yuan Emperor collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the intercalary month in the first year of Yongchang, Emperor Yuan died.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，太子卽皇帝位，大赦，尊所生荀氏爲建安郡君。

translations.literal: On gengyin the heir apparent ascended the emperor's position, great amnesty, honored the birth-giver Lady Xun as Lady of Jian'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day the crown prince took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and raised his birth mother, Lady Xun, to the title of lady of Jian'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 太寧元年春正月癸巳，黃霧四塞，京師火。

translations.literal: Taining first year, spring first month, guisi, yellow fog filled the four directions; the capital had fire.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the first month of the first year of Taining, yellow fog blanketed the land and fires broke out in the capital.

sentences.zh: 李雄使其將李驤、任回寇臺登，將軍司馬玖死之。

translations.literal: Li Xiong sent his generals Li Xiang, Ren Hui to raid Taideng; General Sima Jiu died for it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong dispatched Li Xiang and Ren Hui against Taideng; Sima Jiu, the general sent against them, was killed.

sentences.zh: 越巂太守李釗、漢嘉太守王載以郡叛，降于驤。

translations.literal: Yuegui Administrator Li Zhao, Hanjia Administrator Wang Zai with their commanderies rebelled, surrendered to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The governors Li Zhao of Yuegui and Wang Zai of Hanjia rose with their commands and submitted to Li Xiang.

sentences.zh: 二月，葬元帝于建平陵，帝徒跣至于陵所。

translations.literal: In the second month they buried Yuan Emperor at Jianping Mausoleum; the emperor barefoot went to the mausoleum site.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Emperor Yuan was laid in the Jianping tombs; the new emperor walked the last miles barefoot behind the bier.

sentences.zh: 以特進華恒爲驃騎將軍、都督石頭水陸軍事。

translations.literal: He appointed Specially Advanced Hua Heng as General of Agile Cavalry, Area Commander-in-Chief of Stone Rampart water and land military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Heng, holding the title specially advanced, was named general of agile cavalry and commander of land and river forces at Stone City.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: On yichou yellow fog filled the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day yellow fog closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，隕霜。

translations.literal: On bingyin frost fell.
translations.idiomatic: Frost fell on the bingyin day.

sentences.zh: 壬申，又隕霜，殺穀。

translations.literal: On renshen again frost fell, killing grain.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen frost struck again and blighted the crops.

sentences.zh: 三月戊寅朔，改元，臨軒，停饗宴之禮，懸而不樂。

translations.literal: Third month wuyin new moon, changed era name, faced the balustrade, stopped feasting and banquet rites, suspended but without music.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon wuyin in the third month he changed the reign title, held court from the gallery, canceled banquets, and kept the bells silent.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，隕霜，殺草。

translations.literal: On bingxu frost fell, killing grass.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu frost killed the spring grass.

sentences.zh: 饒安、東光、安陵三縣災，燒七千餘家，死者萬五千人。

translations.literal: Rao'an, Dongguang, Anling three counties had disaster; burned more than seven thousand households; dead fifteen thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: A great fire ravaged Rao'an, Dongguang, and Anling, destroying more than seven thousand homes and killing fifteen thousand people.

sentences.zh: 石勒攻陷下邳，徐州刺史卞敦退保盱眙。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked and captured Xiapi; Xuzhou Inspector Bian Dun retreated to guard Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le took Xiapi, forcing Bian Dun, the governor of Xuzhou, to fall back to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 王敦獻皇帝信璽一紐。

translations.literal: Wang Dun presented the emperor's credence seal, one cord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun presented one of the imperial bronze credence seals.

sentences.zh: 敦將謀篡逆，諷朝廷徵己，帝乃手詔征之。

translations.literal: Dun was about to plot usurpation and rebellion; he hinted to the court to summon himself; the emperor then personally edict summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Dun prepared treason he hinted that the court should recall him; the emperor answered with his own brush, summoning him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，敦下屯於湖，轉司空王導爲司徒，自領揚州牧。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, Dun came down and encamped at Yu Lake; transferred Minister of Works Wang Dao to Minister of Education; himself took concurrent Yangzhou Shepherd.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wang Dun moved his camp to Yuhu, shifted Wang Dao from minister of works to minister of education, and named himself governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 巴東監軍柳純爲敦所害。

translations.literal: Badong Army Supervisor Liu Chun was killed by Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chun, the army supervisor in Badong, was murdered on Wang Dun's orders.

sentences.zh: 以尚書陳昣爲都督幽平二州諸軍事、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Secretary Chen Zhen as Area Commander-in-Chief of You and Ping two states' military affairs, Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen of the secretariat was named area commander for You and Ping and governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，京師大水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the capital had great water.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was inundated in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 李驤等寇寧州，刺史王遜遣將姚岳距戰于堂狼，大破之。

translations.literal: Li Xiang and others raided Ningzhou; Inspector Wang Xun sent general Yao Yue to resist battle at Tanglang, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang invaded Ningzhou; Wang Xun, the governor, sent Yao Yue to meet him at Tanglang and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 梁碩攻陷交州，刺史王諒死之。

translations.literal: Liang Shuo attacked and captured Jiaozhou; Inspector Wang Liang died for it.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shuo overran Jiaozhou, and Governor Wang Liang fell in the defense.

sentences.zh: 六月壬子，立皇后庾氏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month on renzi he established Empress Lady Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the sixth month he invested Lady Yu of the Yu clan as empress.

sentences.zh: 平南將軍陶侃遣參軍高寶攻梁碩，斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Tao Kan sent aide Gao Bao to attack Liang Shuo, beheaded him, transmitted the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan, the general who pacifies the south, sent his aide Gao Bao against Liang Shuo, executed him, and sent the head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 進侃位征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He advanced Kan's position to Grand General Who Conquers the South, Opening Office with Ceremonial Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan was promoted to grand general who conquers the south with an independent headquarters equated to the three highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙子朔，震太極殿柱。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, bingzi new moon, lightning struck the Grand Ultimate Hall's pillars.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon bingzi in the seventh month lightning shattered a pillar of the Grand Ultimate Hall.

sentences.zh: 是月，劉曜攻陳安於隴城，滅之。

translations.literal: That month Liu Yao attacked Chen An at Longcheng, destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Yao stormed Longcheng, destroyed Chen An, and annexed his domain.

sentences.zh: 八月，以安北將軍郗鑒爲尚書令。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he appointed General Who Guards the North Xi Jian as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Xi Jian, general who guards the north, became director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 石勒將石季龍攻陷青州，刺史曹嶷遇害。

translations.literal: Shi Le's general Shi Jilong attacked and captured Qingzhou; Inspector Cao Yi met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu seized the province of Qingzhou and killed Cao Yi, its governor.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，王敦以其兄征南大將軍含爲征東大將軍、都督揚州江西諸軍事。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, Wang Dun because his elder brother Grand General Who Conquers the South Han was made Grand General Who Conquers the East, Area Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou Jiangxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wang Dun gave his brother Wang Han, the grand general who conquers the south, the posts of grand general who conquers the east and commander of all forces west of the Yangzi in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以軍國饑乏，調刺史以下米各有差。

translations.literal: Because army and state were hungry and depleted, he levied grain from inspectors downward, each with differences.
translations.idiomatic: With army and treasury empty, he requisitioned grain from every governor downward on a graded scale.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月丁丑，帝臨朝，停饗宴之禮，懸而不樂。

translations.literal: Second year, spring first month, dingchou, the emperor faced the court, stopped feasting and banquet rites, suspended but without music.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the first month of the second year he held court without feasts or music.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，赦五歲刑以下。

translations.literal: On gengchen he pardoned punishments of five years and below.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day he remitted sentences of five years or less.

sentences.zh: 術人李脫造妖書惑衆，斬于建康市。

translations.literal: Technician Li Tuo made occult writings deluding the multitude; beheaded at Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Li Tuo, who forged seditious tracts, was executed in the marketplace at Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 石勒將石季龍寇兗州，刺史劉遐自彭城退保泗口。

translations.literal: Shi Le's general Shi Jilong raided Yanzhou; Inspector Liu Xia from Pengcheng retreated to guard Sikou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu struck Yanzhou, and Liu Xia withdrew from Pengcheng to hold the mouth of the Si River.

sentences.zh: 三月，劉曜將康平寇魏興，及南陽。

translations.literal: In the third month Liu Yao's general Kang Ping raided Weixing, reaching Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Kang Ping, a general of Liu Yao, raided Weixing and pushed into Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，王敦矯詔拜其子應爲武衛將軍，兄含爲驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, Wang Dun forged an edict appointing his son Ying as Martial Guards General, elder brother Han as Grand General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wang Dun forged an edict naming his son Wang Ying martial guards general and his brother Wang Han grand general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 帝所親信常從督公乘雄、冉曾並爲敦所害。

translations.literal: The emperor's trusted intimate constant-follow supervisors Gongcheng Xiong, Ran Zeng together were killed by Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Gongcheng Xiong and Ran Zeng, the trusted bodyguard officers at the emperor's side, were murdered on Wang Dun's orders.

sentences.zh: 六月，敦將舉兵內向，帝密知之，乃乘巴滇駿馬微行，至于湖，陰察敦營壘而出。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, when Dun was about to raise troops inward, the emperor secretly knew it; then riding Ba-Dian swift horses in disguise, went to Yu Lake, secretly inspected Dun's camps and ramparts and came out.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, learning that Wang Dun meant to march on the capital, the emperor rode a swift Bashu horse in disguise to Yuhu, spied on the rebel camp, and slipped away unseen.

sentences.zh: 有軍士疑帝非常人。

translations.literal: There were soldiers who suspected the emperor was not an ordinary person.
translations.idiomatic: Some sentries sensed that he was no common traveler.

sentences.zh: 又敦正書寢，夢日環其城，驚起曰：「此必黃須鮮卑奴來也。

translations.literal: Moreover Dun was napping over documents, dreamed the sun circled his city; startled he rose, saying: "This must be the yellow-bearded Xianbei slave coming.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Dun, napping over his desk, dreamed that the sun ringed his camp; he started up and cried that the yellow-bearded Xianbei dog had come.

sentences.zh: 」帝母荀氏，燕代人，帝狀類外氏，鬚黃，敦故謂帝云。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mother Lady Xun was a Yan-dai person; the emperor's appearance resembled the maternal side; beard yellow; therefore Dun called the emperor thus.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's mother, Lady Xun, came from the northern frontier, and he resembled her kin in his yellow beard—hence Wang Dun's slur."

sentences.zh: 於是使五騎物色追帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent five riders to search out and pursue the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched five horsemen to hunt him down.

sentences.zh: 帝亦馳去，馬有遺糞，輒以水灌之。

translations.literal: The emperor also galloped off; when the horse left dung, each time he poured water on it.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped on, and whenever the mount dropped dung he washed the trail away with water.

sentences.zh: 見逆旅賣食嫗，以七寶鞭與之，曰：「後有騎來，可以此示也。

translations.literal: Seeing an innkeeper old woman selling food, he gave her a seven-jeweled whip, saying: "If riders come later, you may show them this."
translations.idiomatic: At a roadside inn he gave the old proprietress a jeweled riding crop and told her, "Show this to anyone who rides after me."

sentences.zh: 」俄而追者至，問嫗。

translations.literal: " Soon pursuers arrived and questioned the old woman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the pursuers arrived and questioned her.

sentences.zh: 嫗曰：「去巳遠矣。

translations.literal: " The old woman said: "He has already gone far."
translations.idiomatic: "He is long gone by now," she said.

sentences.zh: 」因以鞭示之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she showed them the whip.
translations.idiomatic: She handed them the crop.

sentences.zh: 五騎傳玩，稽留遂久，又見馬糞冷，以爲信遠而止不追。

translations.literal: " The five riders passed it around to admire it, lingered thus long; again seeing the horse dung cold, they thought it trustworthy that he was far and stopped not pursuing.
translations.idiomatic: The five men passed the whip from hand to hand, wasting time; finding the droppings cold, they believed he was far ahead and gave up the chase.

sentences.zh: 帝僅而獲免。

translations.literal: " The emperor barely thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: So the emperor barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，加司徒王導大都督、假節，領揚州刺史，以丹陽尹溫嶠爲中壘將軍，與右將軍卞敦守石頭，以光祿勳應詹爲護軍將軍、假節、督朱雀橋南諸軍事，以尚書令郗鑒行衛將軍、都督從駕諸軍事，以中書監庾亮領左衛將軍，以尚書卞壼行中軍將軍。

translations.literal: On dingmao he added Minister of Education Wang Dao as Grand Area Commander-in-Chief, with credential staff, concurrent Yangzhou Inspector; appointed Danyang Intendant Wen Qiao as General of the Central Rampart, together with General of the Right Bian Dun to guard Stone Rampart; appointed Supernumerary Minister Ying Zhan as General Who Guards the Army, with credential staff, supervising all military affairs south of the Zhuque Bridge; appointed Director of the Secretariat Xi Jian to act as Guards General, Area Commander-in-Chief of all armies attending the chariot; appointed Palace Secretary Yu Liang to take concurrent Left Guards General; appointed Secretary Bian Kun to act as Central Army General.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Wang Dao became grand commander with the imperial baton and kept the Yangzhou governorship; Wen Qiao, intendant of Danyang, was named general of the central rampart to hold Stone City with Bian Dun, general of the right; Ying Zhan took charge of the southern approaches to the Zhuque Bridge; Xi Jian directed the escort forces; Yu Liang led the left guard; Bian Kun commanded the central army.

sentences.zh: 徵平北將軍、徐州刺史王邃，平西將軍、豫州刺史祖約，北中郎將、兗州刺史劉遐，奮武將軍、臨淮太守蘇峻，奮威將軍、廣陵太守陶瞻等還衛京師。

translations.literal: He summoned General Who Pacifies the North, Xuzhou Inspector Wang Sui, General Who Pacifies the West, Yuzhou Inspector Zu Yue, General of the Northern Center, Yanzhou Inspector Liu Xia, General Who Rouses Might, Linhuai Administrator Su Jun, General Who Rouses Might, Guangling Administrator Tao Zhan and others to return and guard the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Wang Sui, Zu Yue, Liu Xia, Su Jun, Tao Zhan, and other frontier commanders to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝次於中堂。

translations.literal: The emperor encamped at the Central Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He took station in the central hall of the palace.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬申朔，敦遣其兄含及錢鳳、周撫、鄧岳等水陸五萬，至于南岸。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, renshen new moon, Dun sent his elder brother Han together with Qian Feng, Zhou Fu, Deng Yue and others, fifty thousand by water and land, reaching the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon renshen in the seventh month Wang Dun sent Wang Han, Qian Feng, Zhou Fu, and Deng Yue with fifty thousand men across land and water to the south bank of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠移屯水北，燒朱雀桁，以挫其鋒。

translations.literal: Wen Qiao shifted encampment north of the water, burned the Zhuque pontoon, thereby to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao moved his camp north of the river and burned the Zhuque bridge to check the rebel advance.

sentences.zh: 帝躬率六軍，出次南皇堂。

translations.literal: The emperor personally led the six armies, went out and encamped at the South Imperial Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He led the six hosts in person and drew up his lines at the southern imperial hall.

sentences.zh: 至癸酉夜，募壯士，遣將軍段秀、中軍司馬曹渾、左衛參軍陳嵩、鐘寅等甲卒千人渡水，掩其未備。

translations.literal: Reaching guiyou night, he recruited stalwart men, dispatched General Duan Xiu, Central Army Major Cao Hun, Left Guard aide Chen Song, Zhong Yin and others, armored soldiers one thousand, to cross the water, surprise them unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of guiyou he chose a thousand picked men under Duan Xiu, Cao Hun, Chen Song, and Zhong Yin to cross the river and strike before dawn.

sentences.zh: 平旦，戰于越城，大破之，斬其前鋒將何康。

translations.literal: At dawn, they battled at Yuecheng, greatly defeated them, beheaded their vanguard general He Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they routed the enemy at Yuecheng and slew the van leader He Kang.

sentences.zh: 王敦憤惋而死。

translations.literal: Wang Dun in resentment and grief died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun died of rage and shame.

sentences.zh: 前宗正虞潭起義師于會稽。

translations.literal: Former Director of the Imperial Clan Yu Tan raised righteous troops at Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tan, the former director of the imperial clan, raised loyal forces in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 沈充帥萬餘人來會含等，庚辰，築壘于陵口。

translations.literal: Shen Chong led over ten thousand to join Han and the others; on gengchen they built ramparts at Lingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chong brought more than ten thousand men to reinforce Wang Han; on the gengchen day they threw up earthworks at Lingkou.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，劉遐、蘇峻等帥精卒萬人以至，帝夜見，勞之，賜將士各有差。

translations.literal: On dinghai Liu Xia, Su Jun and others led crack troops ten thousand to arrive; the emperor received them by night, consoled them, bestowed on generals and soldiers each with differences.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Liu Xia and Su Jun marched in ten thousand veterans; the emperor met them at night, thanked them, and rewarded the ranks according to merit.

sentences.zh: 義興人周蹇殺敦所署太守劉芳，平西將軍祖約逐敦所署淮南太守任台于壽春。

translations.literal: A Yixing man Zhou Jian killed the Administrator Liu Fang whom Dun had appointed; General Who Pacifies the West Zu Yue drove Dun's appointed Huainan Administrator Ren Tai to flight at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixing Zhou Jian slew Liu Fang, Wang Dun's puppet governor, while Zu Yue chased Ren Tai, the bogus governor of Huainan, back toward Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 乙未，賊衆濟水，護軍將軍應詹帥建威將軍趙胤等距戰，不利。

translations.literal: On yiwei the rebel host forded the water; General Who Guards the Army Ying Zhan led General Who Establishes Might Zhao Yin and others to resist battle, unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the rebels crossed the river; Ying Zhan and Zhao Yin met them but were driven back.

sentences.zh: 賊至宣陽門，北中郎將劉遐、蘇峻等自南塘橫擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The rebels reached Xuanyang Gate; General of the Northern Center Liu Xia, Su Jun and others from the South Embankment struck crosswise, greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanyang Gate Liu Xia and Su Jun swung out from the south levee and shattered the rebel line.

sentences.zh: 劉遐又破沈充于青溪。

translations.literal: Liu Xia again defeated Shen Chong at Qingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia then crushed Shen Chong at Qingxi.

sentences.zh: 丙申，賊燒營宵遁。

translations.literal: On bingshen the rebels burned camp and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: That night the rebels torched their camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 丁西，帝還宮，大赦，惟敦黨不原。

translations.literal: On dingxi, the emperor returned to the palace, great amnesty, only Dun's faction not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He re-entered the palace, ordered a general amnesty, and withheld mercy only from Wang Dun's faction.

sentences.zh: 於是分遣諸將追其黨與，悉平之。

translations.literal: Thereupon separately dispatched various generals to pursue their partisans, all pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals to run down every accomplice until the rising was stamped out.

sentences.zh: 封司徒王導爲始興郡公，邑三千戶，賜絹九千匹；

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Minister of Education Wang Dao as Duke of Shixing commandery, fief three thousand households, bestowed silk nine thousand bolts;
translations.idiomatic: The court enfeoffed Wang Dao as duke of Shixing with three thousand households and nine thousand bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹溫嶠建寧縣公，尚書卞壼建興縣公，中書監庾亮永昌縣公，北中郎將劉遐泉陵縣公，奮武將軍蘇峻邵陵縣公，邑各一千八百戶，絹各五千四百匹；

translations.literal: Danyang Intendant Wen Qiao as Duke of Jianning county, Secretary Bian Kun as Duke of Jianxing county, Palace Secretary Yu Liang as Duke of Yongchang county, General of the Northern Center Liu Xia as Duke of Quanling county, General Who Rouses Might Su Jun as Duke of Shaoling county, fiefs each one thousand eight hundred households, silk each five thousand four hundred bolts;
translations.idiomatic: The court named Wen Qiao duke of Jianning, Bian Kun duke of Jianxing, Yu Liang duke of Yongchang, Liu Xia duke of Quanling, and Su Jun duke of Shaoling—each with eighteen hundred households and fifty-four hundred bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 尚書令郗鑒高平縣侯，護軍將軍應詹觀陽縣侯，邑各千六百戶，絹各四千八百匹；

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Xi Jian as Marquis of Gaoping county, General Who Guards the Army Ying Zhan as Marquis of Guanyang county, fiefs each one thousand six hundred households, silk each four thousand eight hundred bolts;
translations.idiomatic: The court made Xi Jian marquis of Gaoping and Ying Zhan marquis of Guanyang, each with sixteen hundred households and forty-eight hundred bolts;

sentences.zh: 建威將軍趙胤湘南縣侯，右將軍卞敦益陽縣侯，邑各千六百戶，絹各三千二百匹。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might Zhao Yin as Marquis of Xiangnan county, General of the Right Bian Dun as Marquis of Yiyang county, fiefs each one thousand six hundred households, silk each three thousand two hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Zhao Yin marquis of Xiangnan and Bian Dun marquis of Yiyang, each with sixteen hundred households and thirty-two hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其餘封賞各有差。

translations.literal: The rest of enfeoffments and rewards each had differences.
translations.idiomatic: Other officers received graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，以司徒王導爲太保、領司徒，太宰、西陽王羕領太尉，應詹爲平南將軍、都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史，劉遐爲監淮北諸軍事、徐州刺史，庾亮爲護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, he appointed Minister of Education Wang Dao as Grand Guardian, concurrent Minister of Education; Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xiyang Yang concurrent Grand Commandant; Ying Zhan as General Who Pacifies the South, Area Commander-in-Chief of Jiangzhou military affairs, Jiangzhou Inspector; Liu Xia as Supervisor of Huai-north military affairs, Xuzhou Inspector; Yu Liang as General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wang Dao was made grand guardian while keeping the ministry of education; Sima Yang added the grand commandancy; Ying Zhan took Jiangzhou; Liu Xia oversaw the Huai front as Xuzhou governor; Yu Liang became general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 詔王敦羣從一無所問。

translations.literal: He ordered that Wang Dun's entire kin by marriage be questioned nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a general pardon for Wang Dun's collateral kin.

sentences.zh: 是時，石勒將石生屯洛陽，豫州刺史祖約退保壽陽。

translations.literal: At this time Shi Le's general Shi Sheng encamped at Luoyang; Yuzhou Inspector Zu Yue retreated to guard Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the general Shi Sheng held Luoyang, and Zu Yue pulled back to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬子，帝謁建平陵，從大祥之禮。

translations.literal: On renzi the emperor visited Jianping Mausoleum, following the great auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he performed the great felicity rites at his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 梁水太守爨亮、盜竊州太守李逷以興古叛，降于李雄。

translations.literal: Liangshui Administrator Cuan Liang and Ningzhou Administrator Li Ti with Xinggu rebelled, surrendered to Li Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: The administrators Cuan Liang of Liangshui and Li Ti of Ningzhou rose in the district of Xinggu and went over to Li Xiong.

sentences.zh: 沈充故將顧颺反於武康，攻燒城邑，州縣討斬之。

translations.literal: Shen Chong's former general Gu Yang rebelled at Wukang, attacked and burned cities and towns; prefectures and counties campaigned and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yang, once a subordinate of Shen Chong, mutinied at Wukang and burned towns until the local forces cut him down.

sentences.zh: 三年春二月戊辰，復三族刑，惟不及婦人。

translations.literal: Third year, spring second month wuchen, he restored the three-clans punishment, only not reaching women.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year he revived collective punishment of three generations, exempting women.

sentences.zh: 三月，幽州刺史段末波卒，以弟牙嗣。

translations.literal: In the third month Youzhou Inspector Duan Mobo died; his younger brother Ya succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The governor Duan Mobo of Youzhou died; his brother Duan Ya inherited the command.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，立皇子衍爲皇太子，大赦，增文武位二等，大酺三日，賜鰥寡孤獨帛，人二匹。

translations.literal: On wuchen he established the imperial son Yan as imperial heir apparent, great amnesty, increased civil and military ranks two grades, great feast three days, bestowed on widowers, widows, orphans, solitaries silk, two bolts each.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen he named Sima Yan crown prince, proclaimed amnesty, raised officials two steps, feasted the realm for three days, and gave two bolts of silk to every helpless household.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，徵處士臨海任旭、會稽虞喜並爲博士。

translations.literal: On guisi he summoned recluses Ren Xu of Linhai and Yu Xi of Kuaiji together as erudites.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he called the scholars Ren Xu and Yu Xi to court as doctors.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，詔曰：「大事初定，其命惟新。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, an edict said: "The great matter is newly settled; its commands must be fresh.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he decreed, "The realm is only just steadied; every ordinance must be made new."

sentences.zh: 其令太宰司徒巳下，詣都坐參議政道，諸所因革，務盡事中。

translations.literal: Let the Grand Preceptor and Minister of Education downward go to the capital seat to join deliberation on government ways; whatever should be continued or reformed, strive to hit the mean in affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Let every minister from the grand preceptor down meet in the capital office to debate policy—what to keep, what to change—and aim always at the balanced course."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「湌直言，引亮正，想羣賢達吾此懷矣。

translations.literal: " Again an edict said: "Feast on straight words, draw in bright correctness; I trust the host of worthies will reach this mind of mine."
translations.idiomatic: A second edict urged, "Welcome blunt counsel and upright remonstrance; I count on you gentlemen to read my heart."

sentences.zh: 予違汝弼，堯舜之相君臣也。

translations.literal: "When I err, you correct me"—such was the minister-lord relation of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: "When I err, you correct me"—that was how Yao and Shun treated their ministers."

sentences.zh: 吾雖虛闇，庶不距逆耳之談。

translations.literal: "Though I am empty and dim, I hope not to reject talk that stings the ear."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am a dull man, I will not shut my ears to what hurts."

sentences.zh: 稷契之任，君居之矣。

translations.literal: "The burden of Ji and Xie—sirs, you stand in their place."
translations.idiomatic: You hold the burden that once fell to Ji and Xie."

sentences.zh: 望共勖之。

translations.literal: "Hope together you will encourage one another in this."
translations.idiomatic: I look to you to press one another to this duty."

sentences.zh: 」己亥，雨雹。

translations.literal: " On jihai, rain hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hail fell on jihai.

sentences.zh: 石勒將石良寇兗州，刺史檀贇力戰，死之。

translations.literal: Shi Le's general Shi Liang raided Yanzhou; Inspector Tan Yun fought with strength, died for it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liang struck Yanzhou; Tan Yun, the governor, fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 將軍李矩等並衆潰而歸，石勒盡陷司、兗、豫三州之地。

translations.literal: Generals Li Ju and others together with hosts scattered and returned; Shi Le entirely captured Si, Yan, Yu three provinces' lands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju and the other generals broke and fled, and Shi Le overran the provinces of Si, Yan, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 五月，以征南大將軍陶侃爲征西大將軍、都督荊湘雍梁四州諸軍事、荊州刺史，王舒爲安南將軍、都督廣州諸軍事、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he appointed Grand General Who Conquers the South Tao Kan as Grand General Who Conquers the West, Area Commander-in-Chief of Jing, Xiang, Yong, Liang four states' military affairs, Jingzhou Inspector; Wang Shu as General Who Guards the South, Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou military affairs, Guangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Tao Kan became grand general who conquers the west, commanding Jing, Xiang, Yong, and Liang, while Wang Shu took Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，石勒將石季龍攻劉曜將劉岳於新安，陷之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Shi Le's general Shi Jilong attacked Liu Yao's general Liu Yue at Xin'an, captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Shi Hu defeated Liu Yue at Xin'an for Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 以廣州刺史王舒爲都督湘州諸軍事、湘州刺史，湘州刺史劉顗爲平越中郎將、都督廣州諸軍事、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He appointed Guangzhou Inspector Wang Shu as Area Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou military affairs, Xiangzhou Inspector; Xiangzhou Inspector Liu Yi as General Who Pacifies the Yue, Area Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou military affairs, Guangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu was shifted to Xiangzhou while Liu Yi took Guangzhou and the Yue command.

sentences.zh: 大旱，自正月不雨，至于是月。

translations.literal: Great drought; from the first month it did not rain until this month.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought had gripped the land since the first month without rain.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛未，以尚書令郗鑒爲車騎將軍、都督青兗二州諸軍事、假節，鎮廣陵，領軍將軍卞壼爲尚書令。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, xinwei, he appointed Director of the Secretariat Xi Jian as General of Chariots and Cavalry, Area Commander-in-Chief of Qing and Yan two states' military affairs, with credential staff, garrisoning Guangling; Army Commandant Bian Kun as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the seventh month Xi Jian became general of chariots and cavalry on the northern front at Guangling, and Bian Kun succeeded him as director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「三恪二王，世代之所重；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The three reverent guests and the two kings are what generations have honored;
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed, "The three guest houses and the two royal houses are the honor of every age;"

sentences.zh: 興滅繼絕，政道之所先。

translations.literal: raising the fallen and continuing the cut off is what government way puts first."
translations.idiomatic: to restore fallen lines is the first duty of government."

sentences.zh: 又宗室哲王有功勳于大晉受命之際者，佐命功臣，碩德名賢，三祖所與共維大業，咸開國胙土、誓同山河者，而並廢絕，禋祀不傳，甚用懷傷。

translations.literal: "Also imperial clan wise princes who had merit and labor at Great Jin's receiving-the-mandate juncture, adjutant mandate meritorious ministers, great virtue famous worthies, those the three ancestors together with upheld the great enterprise, all who opened states and feoffed soil, swore same as mountains and rivers—yet together were cut off and ended, smoke sacrifice not transmitted—this deeply wounds the heart."
translations.idiomatic: Those princes and ministers who helped found Jin, received fiefs, and swore oaths with the throne have seen their lines die out and their sacrifices cease—this grieves me deeply."

sentences.zh: 主者其祥議諸應立後者以聞。

translations.literal: "Let those in charge carefully deliberate whom among those who ought to have heirs established, and report."
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministries report which lines deserve heirs."

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「郊祀天地，帝王之重事。

translations.literal: " Again an edict said: "Suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth is emperors' weighty affair."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict added, "The suburban rites to Heaven and Earth are the sovereign's greatest duty."

sentences.zh: 自中興以來，惟南郊，未曾北郊，四時五郊之禮都不復設，五嶽、四瀆、名山、大川載在祀典應望秩者，悉廢而未舉。

translations.literal: "Since the restoration, only the southern suburb has been performed; the northern suburb has never been performed; the four seasons and five suburbs' rites all are not again established; the five marchmounts, four rivers, famous mountains, great streams recorded in the sacrifice canon that ought to receive ranked offerings, all are abolished and not yet raised."
translations.idiomatic: Since the court moved south we have sacrificed only at the southern suburb; the northern rite and the seasonal five-suburb liturgy have lapsed, and offerings to the great mountains and rivers have not been restored."

sentences.zh: 主者其依舊詳處。」

translations.literal: "Let those in charge according to old precedents deliberate and settle."
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministries draft a restoration plan on old precedents."

sentences.zh: 八月，詔曰：「昔周武克殷，封比干之墓；

translations.literal: " In the eighth month an edict said: "Formerly Zhou Wu conquered Yin, enfeoffed Bi Gan's tomb;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he cited how King Wu of Zhou tended Bi Gan's tomb after conquering Yin;

sentences.zh: 漢高過趙，錄樂毅之後，追顯旣往，以勸將來也。

translations.literal: Han Gao passed Zhao, recorded Yue Yi's posterity—pursuing display of what is already past, thereby to encourage what is yet to come."
translations.idiomatic: and how Han Gaozu honored the descendants of Yue Yi in Zhao—to glorify the past and hearten the future."

sentences.zh: 吳時將相名賢之胄，有能纂修家訓，又忠孝仁義，靜己守眞，不聞于時者，州郡中正亟以名聞，勿有所遺。」

translations.literal: "Of Wu times' generals and ministers' famous worthies' descendants, those able to compile and cultivate family instructions, moreover loyal, filial, benevolent, righteous, quieting self and guarding truth, not heard of in their time—let prefectures and counties' central rectifiers urgently by name report, do not let any be missed."
translations.idiomatic: If any descendant of Wu's great houses keeps the family teachings in loyalty, filial piety, and integrity yet lives in obscurity, the local rectifiers shall send their names at once and omit none."

sentences.zh: 閏月，以尚書左僕射荀崧爲光祿大夫、錄尚書事，尚書鄧攸爲尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, he appointed Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Xun Song as Supernumerary Minister, Recorder of Secretariat Affairs; Secretary Deng You as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Xun Song became supernumerary minister and recorder of the secretariat, and Deng You became left vice director.

sentences.zh: 壬午，帝不悆，召太宰、西陽王羕，司徒王導，尚書令卞壼，車騎將軍郗鑒，護軍將軍庾亮，領軍將軍陸曄，丹陽尹溫嶠並受遺詔，輔太子。

translations.literal: On renwu the emperor was unwell; he summoned Grand Preceptor, Prince of Xiyang Yang, Minister of Education Wang Dao, Director of the Secretariat Bian Kun, General of Chariots and Cavalry Xi Jian, General Who Guards the Army Yu Liang, Army Commandant Lu Ye, Danyang Intendant Wen Qiao together to receive testamentary edict, to assist the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, failing in health, he called Sima Yang, Wang Dao, Bian Kun, Xi Jian, Yu Liang, Lu Ye, and Wen Qiao to the bedside and entrusted them with the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：「自古有死，賢聖所同，壽夭窮達，歸于一概，亦何足特痛哉！

translations.literal: On dinghai an edict said: "From antiquity there is death; sages and worthies share the same; long life, early death, blocked and open, return to one norm—what is sufficient especially to pain!"
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day he wrote, "Death comes to all, wise or foolish; long or short life ends the same—there is no cause for singular grief!"

sentences.zh: 朕枕疾已久，常慮忽然。

translations.literal: "I pillow-illness long already, always fear sudden end."
translations.idiomatic: I have long been bedridden and fear a sudden end."

sentences.zh: 仰惟祖宗洪基，不能克終堂構，大恥未雪，百姓塗炭，所以有慨耳。

translations.literal: "Looking up to the ancestors' great foundation, I am unable to complete the hall's frame; great shame not yet washed; the hundred surnames smeared in mud and charcoal—therefore I have sighing only."
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that I cannot finish the house my ancestors built, that shame to the north remains unavenged, and that the people still suffer—that is what stirs my heart."

sentences.zh: 不幸之日，斂以時服，一遵先度，務從簡約，勞衆崇飾，皆勿爲也。

translations.literal: "On the unlucky day, enshroud with seasonal garments, one follow former measures, strive to follow simplicity; toil the multitude and exalt ornament—none shall be done."
translations.idiomatic: When I die, dress me in the robes fit to the season, follow the old sumptuary rules, and do not burden the people with lavish display."

sentences.zh: 衍以幼弱，猥當大重，當賴忠賢，訓而成之。

translations.literal: "Yan being young and weak, meanly bears the great weight; he ought to rely on loyal worthies, instruct and complete him."
translations.idiomatic: Yan is still a child yet must bear the throne; lean on loyal men to train him."

sentences.zh: 昔周公匡輔成王，霍氏擁育孝昭，義行前典，功冠二代，豈非宗臣之道乎？

translations.literal: "Formerly the Duke of Zhou aided and assisted King Cheng; the Huo clan embraced and nurtured filial Zhao—righteousness walked former canons, merit crowned two generations—is this not the way of imperial ministers?"
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou raised King Cheng, and Huo Guang guarded young Zhaodi—does that not show the way of a pillar of the house?"

sentences.zh: 凡此公卿，時之望也。

translations.literal: "All these dukes and ministers are the age's expectation."
translations.idiomatic: You are the men the age looks to."

sentences.zh: 敬聽顧命，任託付之重，同心斷金，以謀王室。

translations.literal: "Respectfully hear the testamentary charge, bear the weight of entrusted commission, with one heart cut metal, thereby to plan for the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: Hear my will, share the burden I lay on you, and like metal cut by one stroke plan for the house of Jin."

sentences.zh: 諸方嶽征鎮，刺史將守，皆朕扞城，推轂於外，雖事有內外，其致一也。

translations.literal: "The various regional shepherds, conquerors, garrisoners, inspectors, generals, and guards are all my city walls, pushing the chariot outside; although affairs have inner and outer, their reaching is one."
translations.idiomatic: Every governor and general is a wall of the throne; though some serve at court and some in the field, your charge is one."

sentences.zh: 故不有行者，誰扞牧圉？

translations.literal: "Therefore without those who march, who guards the herds and pastures?"
translations.idiomatic: Without armies in the field, who guards the marches?"

sentences.zh: 譬若脣齒，表裏相資。

translations.literal: "It is like lips and teeth, outer and inner aiding each other."
translations.idiomatic: You are lip and tooth to one another."

sentences.zh: 宜戮力一心，若合符契，思美焉之美，以緝事爲期。

translations.literal: "Ought join strength one heart, as if matching tally seals, thinking of the beauty of "how beautiful"—take orderly governance as the term."
translations.idiomatic: Work as one, match your efforts like tally halves, and aim at the good order the Odes praise."

sentences.zh: 百辟卿士，其總己以聽于冢宰，保祐沖幼，弘濟艱難，永令祖宗之靈，寧于九天之上，則朕沒于地下，無恨黃泉。」

translations.literal: "Hundred lords and ministers, let them gather themselves to listen to the Grand Steward, protect the tender young, broadly aid hardship and peril, forever letting the ancestors' spirits rest in the nine heavens above—then I, having perished below ground, will have no regret in the yellow springs."
translations.idiomatic: All officers shall obey the chief minister, guard the boy emperor, and carry the state through danger so the spirits of our ancestors may rest easy; then I shall lie in the earth without regret."

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝崩于東堂，年二十七，葬武平陵，廟號肅祖。

translations.literal: On wuzi the emperor collapsed in the Eastern Hall, age twenty-seven; buried at Wuping Mausoleum; temple name Suzu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eastern hall on wuzi at twenty-seven, was buried at Wuping, and received the temple name Suzu.

sentences.zh: 帝聰明有機斷，尤精物理。

translations.literal: The emperor was clever and had decisive judgment, especially refined in the patterns of things.
