translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted, resolute, and keenly observant of how things work.

sentences.zh: 于時兵凶歲饑，死疫過半，虛弊旣甚，事極艱虞。

translations.literal: At that time weapons were fierce, years famine, death and pestilence more than half; emptiness and exhaustion already extreme, affairs reached utmost hardship and peril.
translations.idiomatic: War, famine, and plague had carried off more than half the people; the realm was exhausted and peril pressed from every side.

sentences.zh: 屬王敦挾震主之威，將移神器。

translations.literal: Just when Wang Dun bore the awesomeness that shakes the ruler, about to shift the divine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun then wielded power enough to overshadow the throne and meant to seize the regalia.

sentences.zh: 帝騎驅遵養，以弱制強，潛謀獨斷，廓清大祲。

translations.literal: The emperor on horseback drove compliance and nurture, using weakness to control strength, secret plans alone decided, broadly cleared the great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He temporized, feigned weakness, and struck by secret design until the great peril was swept away.

sentences.zh: 改授荊、湘等四州，以分上流之勢，撥亂反正，強本弱枝。

translations.literal: He reassigned Jing, Xiang and other four provinces, thereby to divide the upper stream's force; set chaos right and returned to correctness, strengthening root and weakening branch.
translations.idiomatic: He carved Jing, Xiang, and neighboring provinces into new commands to break the power of the upper Yangzi, righting the realm and strengthening the center against the regions.

sentences.zh: 雖享國日淺，而規模弘遠矣。

translations.literal: Although enjoying the state days were shallow, yet the pattern and measure were broad and far.
translations.idiomatic: His reign was short, yet his institutions looked far ahead.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：維揚作宇，憑帶洪流，楚江恒戰，方城對敵，不得不推誠將相，以總戎麾。

translations.literal: The historians say: Building a house at Weiyang, girdled by the mighty current, Chu river always at war, Fangcheng facing foes—one could not but extend trust to generals and ministers to grasp the command banners.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: With the capital on the Yangzi, ever threatened from Chu and Fangcheng, the throne had no choice but to put the army in the hands of its generals.

sentences.zh: 樓船萬計，兵倍王室，處其利而無心者，周公其人也。

translations.literal: Ten thousand towered ships, soldiers doubled the royal house; dwelling in its advantage yet without selfish heart—such was the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When fleet and soldiery outmatched the court yet no selfish heart remained, that was the Duke of Zhou's way.

sentences.zh: 威權外假，嫌隙內興，彼有順流之師，此無強籓之援。

translations.literal: Mighty power lent outward, suspicion and rift arising within; they had downstream armies, here no strong screen's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Once power was delegated abroad, suspicion flared within: rebels rode the current downriver while no strong shield stood at court.

sentences.zh: 商逢九亂，堯止八音，明皇負圖，屬在茲日。

translations.literal: Shang met nine disorders, Yao stopped eight sounds—Ming Huang bore the chart, it fell on this day.
translations.idiomatic: As Shang knew nine turmoils and Yao silenced the eight tones, so the "bright sovereign" faced his trial in this hour.

sentences.zh: 運龍韜於掌握，起天旆於江靡，燎其餘燼，有若秋原。

translations.literal: He wielded the dragon stratagem in his palm, raised Heaven's banner on the river's brink, burned their remaining embers as if on an autumn plain.
translations.idiomatic: He held strategy in his hand, raised the imperial banner along the shore, and burned the rebel embers like stubble on an autumn field.

sentences.zh: 去縗絰而踐戎場，斬鯨鯢而拜園闕。

translations.literal: He cast off mourning sashes and trod the battle line, beheaded great monsters and bowed at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: He left mourning for war, struck down the leviathan, and returned to bow at the gate.

sentences.zh: 鎮削威權，州分江漢，覆車不踐。

translations.literal: He trimmed and cut mighty authority, divided provinces along Jiang and Han, so the overturned chariot did not tread the same rut.
translations.idiomatic: He pared back warlord power, split the Jiang–Han command, and kept the cart from the old ruts.

sentences.zh: 貽厥孫謀。

translations.literal: He handed down plans for grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: He left his grandson a blueprint.

sentences.zh: 其後七十餘年，終罹敬道之害。

translations.literal: Afterward seventy-odd years, in the end suffered Jingdao's harm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet seventy years later the house still met the disaster of Huan's revolt.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「興亡在運，非止上流。

translations.literal: Someone said: "Rise and fall lie in fate, not only in the upper stream."
translations.idiomatic: Some say rise and fall ride fate, not the upper river alone.

sentences.zh: 」豈創制不殊，而弘之者異也。

translations.literal: "How is it that founding systems were not different, yet those who enlarged them differed."
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the institutions were the same, but the men who carried them forward were not.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：傾天起害，猛獸呈災。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Heaven-toppling raised harm; fierce beasts displayed calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: Heaven was overthrown and calamity rose; savage beasts showed their fangs.

sentences.zh: 琅邪之子，仁義歸來，龔行趙璧，命箠荊臺。

translations.literal: The son of Langye, benevolence and righteousness returned; reverently he marched with the Zhao jade; he ordered the scourge at the Jing terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Langye brought benevolence and right back to the realm, marched in the manner of a righteous host bearing the sacred charge, and laid the rod to rebellion on the Jing terraces.

sentences.zh: 雲瞻北晦，江望南開。

translations.literal: Clouds gazed north in gloom; the river looked south and opened.
translations.idiomatic: The north lay under lowering clouds; south of the river a new horizon opened.

sentences.zh: 晉陽禦敵，河西全壤。

translations.literal: Jinyang resisted the foe; west of the river the soil was kept whole.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang they turned the enemy; beyond the river the land stayed intact.

sentences.zh: 胡寇雖艱，靈心弗爽。

translations.literal: Though the Hu bandits were hard, the numinous mind did not err.
translations.idiomatic: Though the barbarian hosts pressed hard, the sovereign mind never wavered.

sentences.zh: 三方馳騖，百蠻從響。

translations.literal: The three directions galloped; the hundred barbarians followed the echo.
translations.idiomatic: Armies raced to the three fronts, and the myriad tribes answered the call.

sentences.zh: 寶命還昌，金輝載朗。

translations.literal: The precious mandate returned to splendor; metal radiance shone clear.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred mandate shone again, and the golden virtue of the throne gleamed bright.

sentences.zh: 明后岐嶷，軍書接要。

translations.literal: The bright lord stood wise apart; military documents met at the crucial points.
translations.idiomatic: The brilliant ruler showed precocious judgment, and orders from the field came thick and fast.

sentences.zh: 莽首晨懸，董臍昏燎。

translations.literal: Mang's head hung at dawn; Dong's navel was burned as a lamp at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Like Wang Mang's head hung at dawn and Dong Zhuo's navel burned for a night lamp, the usurpers met their end.

sentences.zh: 厥德不回，餘風可劭。

translations.literal: That virtue did not turn back; the remaining wind can be urged on.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue held true without swerving, and the wind of his example still urges the age onward.
